#1812. Brighton & Hove Albion vs Brentford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 18:08, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 01:19

High-flying Brighton & Hove Albion will welcome Brentford to the Amex Stadium for Sunday's Premier League encounter.

The Seagulls head into the weekend in third spot in the Premier League table, while the Bees start matchday 10 in sixth position.

Brighton are a surprise team in the Premier League title picture after winning six, drawing one and losing two of their nine top-flight matches this term.

Fabian Hurzeler's side demonstrated they are capable of bettering the Premier League's biggest teams in last Saturday's away meeting with Manchester City, which saw Yasin Ayari score the decisive goal in a 1-0 victory as Brighton got revenge for their EFL Cup loss to the Citizens just a few days earlier.

The victory moved them to within two points of second-placed Man City and kept them within five points of leaders Arsenal.

Brighton's domestic success has been made all the more impressive by the fact they are balancing it with a Conference League campaign, in which their latest outing yielded a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Getafe in Thursday's trip to Spain.

After moving up to fifth spot in the league phase, the Seagulls will now return to the familiar surroundings of the Amex Stadium, where they are yet to lose this season after winning five and drawing one of their six home matches in all competitions.

All five of those wins have produced clean sheets and at least three goals, including a statement 5-0 victory in their most recent home outing against rivals Crystal Palace.

Brighton head into Sunday's fixture with an unbeaten Premier League home record against Brentford, having won three and drawn two of their five top-flight meetings at the Amex Stadium.

Brentford, meanwhile, are sitting two points adrift of the top four after winning three, drawing five and losing just one of their nine Premier League games this season.

While the Bees are firmly in the hunt for European football, they returned from the international break with a four-game winless run in all competitions before they got back on track in last Saturday's home clash with Nottingham Forest.

A Nikola Milenkovic own goal sent Keith Andrews's side into the break with a slender advantage, before Igor Thiago scored in a second straight game to wrap up all three points at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The Bees will head on their travels with hopes of recording back-to-back Premier League victories for the first time since beating Aston Villa and Newcastle United at the start of February.

That will be easier said than done for a team that has gone nine consecutive away league games without a win, although they have at least proven to be tough to beat after drawing each of their four Premier League road trips this term.

If they are to claim a long-awaited win, they will have to beat Brighton at the Amex Stadium for the first time since picking up a 2-0 victory in the Championship in September 2016.

The visitors will at least fancy their chances of striking first, having netted the opener in eight of their nine Premier League matches.

Brighton & Hove Albion Premier League form:

Brighton & Hove Albion form (all competitions):

Brighton remain without the services of Kaoru Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas, Zadok Yohanna and Evan Ferguson.

Pascal Struijk and Femi Azeez are making progress in their respective injury recoveries, but Sunday's contest is likely to come too soon for the pair.

Full-back Ferdi Kadioglu, who has missed the last three games with a hip issue, is understood to have a chance of proving his fitness in time for the home fixture.

If he is ready to feature, the Turkey international will likely replace Costinha in what could be the only change made to the side that started last Saturday's win over Man City.

As for the visitors, Andrews has reported no fresh injury concerns, although he is unable to call upon a number of players, including Rico Henry, Kaye Furo, Josh Dasilva and Fabio Carvalho.

Antoni Milambo has been training regularly as he closes in on a return from a long-term injury absence, but he is not expected to be risked at the Amex Stadium.

The Brentford boss will welcome back Yehor Yarmoliuk, who is in contention for a starting spot after serving a three-match ban.

Jaidon Anthony is also pushing for a starting berth after coming off the bench to provide an assist for Thiago's goal in the win over Nottingham Forest.

Brighton & Hove Albion possible starting lineup:

Verbruggen; Kadioglu, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Gross, Andres; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas

Kelleher; Kayode, Ajer, Van den Berg, Lewis-Potter; Yarmoliuk, Janelt; Anthony, Jensen, Schade; Thiago

Brighton have scored at least three goals in each of their five competitive home wins this season, and while Brentford have drawn all four of their away league games this term, we think the Seagulls will make full use of their firepower to extend their unbeaten head-to-head home run with a relatively comfortable victory.

#1811. Roberto De Zerbi explains the simple reason Tottenham lost to Leeds

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi admits Tottenham did not play with the right spirit or character in the second half as they fell to a 1-0 defeat away to Leeds.

Spurs were looking to make it four wins in a row for the first time in more than 1,000 days at Elland Road, but despite a valiant defensive effort, they did not offer any threat in attack and were eventually punished when substitute Noah Okafor struck with just over 10 minutes to play.

De Zerbi’s side competed well in a feisty first half without ever troubling Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford, and felt aggrieved not to have the man advantage after Jayden Bogle escaped punishment for a hefty challenge on Mathys Tel.

Leeds took control after the break, though, and despite De Zerbi turning to his bench to make a triple change in the 65th minute, the visitors were unable to stem the tide of pressure.

Spurs were second best after half-time, and De Zerbi was frank in his assessment of his side’s second-half performance, criticising his players’ spirit, character and physicality.

“I’m sorry for the result, but first of all, I’m sorry for the performance in the second half,” De Zerbi said post-match.

“We didn’t play like a top team, we played without the right spirit, the right character, the right physicality in the duels.”

Spurs had grown into the game after an early wave of Leeds pressure, but were dealt an injury blow shortly before half-time when Tel had to come off after taking a hit to his left Achilles from Bogle.

A four-minute VAR review led to no further action for the Leeds defender, much to the frustration of De Zerbi.

The Spurs boss vented his frustrations on the touchline and will now serve a touchline ban against Ipswich Town after picking up his third yellow card of the season.

On the incident, though, De Zerbi insists he still has full confidence in VAR and said his side could not blame the officials for the result.

“No, I have big confidence in the referee,” De Zerbi said when asked if he would have wanted referee John Brooks to go to the monitor to look at Bogle’s challenge.

“Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR, and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know. But we have confidence, we have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve.”

#1810. Gattuso insists pressure is not on high-flying Lazio against Napoli

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Gennaro Gattuso insists there is no pressure on Lazio ahead of Sunday's clash with Napoli, adding he would be fortunate to even achieve a quarter of what Massimiliano Allegri has done in his career.

Lazio have been the surprise package in Serie A so far this campaign, earning 28 points from their first 10 matches.

In the three-points-for-a-win era (since 2994-95), only four teams had previously reached that tally within 10 games – Juventus (in 2012-13 and 2018-19), Roma (2013-14), Napoli (2017-18 and 2021-22) and AC Milan (2021-22).

Of those six instances, all except Juventus in 2012-13 won their 11th match to reach 31 points.

The Opta supercomputer now assigns the Biancocelesti a 12.3% chance of winning the Scudetto, compared to just a 0.5% hope for Napoli, but Gattuso – who coached the Partenopei between 2019 and 2021, winning the Coppa Italia – sees his side as underdogs.

"It depends on how you look at it. We don't have any pressure on us, especially tomorrow,2 Gattuso said, as quoted by Football Italia.

"We're aware of the fact that we will go to play in a tough stadium against a strong team that is going through a difficult period. It will take humility and for us to be at our best."

Gattuso then added that reaching 40 points – and ensuring they will not get dragged into an unlikely relegation battle – remains the first hurdle for Lazio to clear.

He said: "We have to think game by game, there are 12 points left for us to get, then, once we've hit 40 points, we'll have a big celebration for reaching our first goal."

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 4, 2026

While Gattuso has made a tremendous start to his first campaign in charge of Lazio, Allegri – who coached the former midfielder at Milan – has struggled early on at Napoli.

Allegri surprisingly cancelled his pre-match press conference 10 minutes before it was due to take place on Saturday, with Napoli's players being forced into a training retreat amid rumours surrounding their head coach's future.

In three previous managerial meetings between the duo, all of which came when Gattuso was in charge of Milan and Allegri was with Juventus, the now-Lazio boss has suffered three defeats.

"Max was my captain in Serie B [with Perugia] and then my coach," Gattuso said of Allegri. "History says that I've never won against him.

"I hope to achieve a quarter of what he's achieved. Knowing him, I know that he does not suffer from stress. In moments of difficulty, he always knows the right things to do."

Napoli have picked up 14 points in their first ten Serie A matches this season (W4 D2 L4); they have not lost five of their first 11 league games since 2000-01, while a draw against Lazio would equal their worst start in terms of points (15) since 2007-08.

De Bruyne, who has scored four goals in Serie A this season, is looking to become the second midfielder to reach five goals in the competition in both 2025-26 and 2026-27, after AC Milan's Adrien Rabiot.

The Manchester City legend has scored three goals in his last five Serie A outings, as many as he netted in his previous 18 in the competition.

Isaksen has scored four goals in his last five Serie A appearances, as many goals as he netted in his previous 29 outings in the competition.

He is just one goal from matching his best tally in a Serie A season (five in 30 appearances in 2025-26) and is looking to score in three consecutive league appearances for the first time since a run of four matches between May and June 2023 with Midtjylland.

The Opta supercomputer makes Napoli slight favourites on their own turf, but the omens do not look great for the Partenopei.

Indeed, Napoli have lost their last four Serie A home games against Lazio, their longest home losing streak against a single opponent in the competition.

It is Lazio's joint-longest ongoing away winning streak, inferior only to their run against Empoli (six, also four straight wins versus Genoa).

Additionally, Lazio's six-match winning run in Serie A is their longest since the 2019-20 season, when they achieved 11 successive victories under Simone Inzaghi.

Lazio have also won all five of their away games in Serie A this season; the last team to achieve six wins in their first six away matches was Inter in 2019-20, but the Biancocelesti could become the first team to ever achieve that feat three times, after doing so in 2002-03 and 2017-18.

#1808. Man United news: Lisandro Martinez should not play for the Red Devils again

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 18:31

Ahead of Manchester United's Premier League clash with Aston Villa on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses the 20-time English champions.

The Red Devils are without a win in the Premier League since the end of August but managed to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

If they go and get beaten here, it undoes all the good work from the Roma match. It was just an extraordinary game. Those two goals going in, the Soule goal and then the Malen penalty, and you just thought here we go again.

As Mick McCarthy said, it can get worse. At half time, that was probably as bad as I have felt as a Man United fan for a while. There have been some bad moments over the last 14 or 15 years, but you just thought they were never going to win a game again.

Then you have a turning moment, and it was the Fernandes penalty: he missed it, then the retake, and it goes in. It just takes little moments in football.

Roma have previous in the Champions League this season of not being able to hold on to a lead. It was happening against Real Madrid as well. They must have smelt blood. They must have felt Roma had mistakes in them. It was not Roma's first-choice goalkeeper between the sticks either. They did not test him in the first half at all.

But then the penalty goes in, and you think: what are they made of? Cunha was one that took the game by the scruff of the neck, quite literally late on.

He took his shirt off for the yellow card and then got sent off with a bad tackle late on, but you do not mind that. The fans certainly do not mind seeing that aggression, which has been lacking all season.

Shea Lacey has to come in down the right for this game. Amad Diallo is a good footballer, nice and tidy, but he has not scored a goal in going on a year now, and that is just not good enough. He missed a big one at Chelsea last weekend.

Shea Lacey has to come in down the right. He played that lovely pass to Cunha for the 3-2 goal late on. He was bright, he wanted the ball, and he has to come into the team.

Patrick Dorgu is back in training, and it will be very interesting to see whether he is fit enough to start. If he is, I would like to see a reshuffle at the back: Dorgu at left back, Dalot over to the right, with Yoro and Maguire in the middle.

Martinez is suspended, and Heaven is struggling at the moment. I do not want to go too overboard on Heaven. He has had a lot of criticism, but he is only 20 years old and is just not ready, probably not good enough, to be a starting centre back at Man United at this moment in time, and that is fine. He can supplement the squad.

Carlos Baleba will be facing a lengthy period out. Tielemans as a straight swap, or Santos as an option alongside Kobbie Mainoo. Mbeumo, Cunha and Fernandes: I expect them to start again.

I do not think there will be too many changes, but I would like to see those ones because they just need more down the right, where the fullbacks have struggled this season.

The defeat to Chelsea: Man United played really well in the first half but just could not get that goal. They did get a goal through Cunha that was rightly disallowed for offside, but it was so disappointing at that moment.

The Martinez incident: I said a few weeks ago after his comments about the Champions League game that I did not want him to play for the club again, and I do not want him to play for the club again now. That was unforgivable. He has lost his head. He is going to leave the club, whether that is this summer or the next.

Whether you release him or look to sell him, I do not want Martinez playing for Man United anymore. He has let the club down badly and there is no coming back from that.

Try to get a centre back in January, and next summer Man United need to sign three or four defenders. Can Marcus Rashford get himself fit for this game? Probably unlikely. Luke Shaw is still out. Sesko is still out.

But there is a chance now for them to go and beat Aston Villa, a good Aston Villa side, on Sunday afternoon, and then go into the international break in a positive mood.

I read a report recently that apparently Didier Deschamps has been contacted as a potential name, one that has not been at the forefront of many people's thoughts at this stage.

I still expect Carrick to leave at some point, whether that is after this game, in two months' time, or at the end of the season.

I do not expect Michael Carrick to be the manager of Manchester United for the next five years.

The reports at the moment suggest there would not be an interim, so it is unlikely he will go and then someone be brought in next summer.

It looks like they might try to keep Carrick in the job for as long as possible until they identify that next appointment. I wrote a piece recently about Cesc Fabregas and Man United.

After that Como win in the Champions League, I would like to see Fabregas as a long-term option at Manchester United. Deschamps would be a very interesting candidate as well.

Carrick got his stay of execution last time out. He needed that result, and inside he would have been absolutely buzzing with what he saw in that second half.

Man United cannot go two down in this game. If they go two-nil down, they are in big trouble. They need to score first on Sunday.

Go and get a win, go into the international break with more positivity ahead of the Liverpool game at Anfield straight after. Big games to come: Sporting Lisbon away in the Champions League at the end of the month.

I expect Carrick to stay at the moment. If they get beaten here and it is a bad one, he could go. Really interesting times, but a good win last time out and finally a little bit of positivity.

#1807. Wily veterans and the fountain of youth: The five key battles in Milan vs. Ferencvaros

AC Milan return to Europa League action at San Siro this evening for a must-win game against high-flyers Ferencvaros.

Starting their European campaign with two defeats (vs. Benfica and Bournemouth) and one win last left Milan down in 24th in the table, meaning that they need to turn things around if they are to mount a surge towards the top eight spots.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tonight’s game will be far from straightforward though, as Ferencvaros have taken nine points from nine and therefore sit fourth in the table. They are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and are two points from the summit in their domestic league, with a game in hand to play.

Reports are suggesting that Ruben Amorim will turn to a youthful line-up for this one despite the status of being a must-win game. However, the spine of the team will still be made up of players who must deliver.

Starting with a rather unconventional battle, the one between the two goalkeepers Lorenzo Torriani and Dénes Dibusz could be potentially decisive, for obvious reasons. Ferencvaros have conceded just three goals in their three Europa games so far and just 10 in 10 in the league, and the 35-year-old veteran Dibusz has been a big part of that, even if there has been some rotation.

For Torriani, this is arguably his biggest opportunity in a Milan shirt. His only other start came in a Coppa Italia rout of Sassuolo, while he came off the bench in a Champions League defeat to Liverpool, and in the Bournemouth defeat. This is a huge chance for the 20-year-old to not only show he is a capable deputy in the present, but a potential Mike Maignan successor down the line.

There will also be two crucial duels involving the two Nagys, Oliver and Adam. The former will play at right-back and faces the difficult task of keeping Alphadjo Cisse quiet. The Italian is the Rossoneri’s top scorer this season and will be champing at the bit to build on his hat-trick against RB Salzburg. Oliver Nagy is dangerous going forward though, with two assists in his five starts, so Cisse will have to help out defensively too.

Adam Nagy meanwhile faces the task of stopping Milan’s second-top scorer, Adrien Rabiot. The Frenchman netted his fifth of the season in the derby against Inter, and Amorim has chosen to rely on his experience against an opponent who is also 31 years of age. The Hungarian signed from Spezia in the summer and is best known for his appearances at the 2016, 2020 and 2024 UEFA European Championships for his national team.

Ferencvaros have two main threats that Milan must keep quiet, especially the way that this game could play out with the visitors no doubt keen to contain and counter. Bamidele Yusuf is the first, and the Nigerian is expected to start up front this evening though he can also play and drift wide. He has six goals and three assists in 10 starts this season for the green and whites.

Bamidele Yusuf 🎯#UEL | @Fradi_HU pic.twitter.com/AXnt4XPaSu

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) October 29, 2026

Sanhoun Diawara will have to do his bit to keep Yusuf quiet, but our feeling is that Koni De Winter will take on the man-marking duties just like he did with Inter’s lone striker Marcus Thuram in the derby. The Belgian has been undroppable in a literal sense, so we hope that no signs of fatigue are seen especially in transition, like against Bologna.

The visitors’ other danger man is Kristoffer Zachariassen, who matches Yusuf on nine goal contributions (seven goals, two assists) for the season. The 32-year-old Norwegian has plenty of experience and an eye for goal from the attacking midfield role, though his heat maps show he tends to drift to the right too.

So, it will be down to Ardon Jashari to keep tabs on him. Amorim and Milan are still waiting for the Swiss to put together a good run of solid starts after his arrival from Club Brugge for over €30m, and this is the kind of game that he needs to seize control of and dominate to show he is capable of being the anchor man, especially with Luka Modric’s retirement surely not far away.

#1806. VAR error! Why Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty against Hull despite Kai Havertz offside

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal were denied a penalty in their Premier League encounter against Hull City on Saturday after a “very controversial VAR intervention”.

The Gunners, who were on top for much of the first half at the Emirates Stadium, thought they have have a chance to score from 12 yards when Kai Havertz went down in the penalty box under challenge from visiting defender Nobel Mendy.

Play continued but the incident was assessed by VAR for a number of minutes, before referee Farai Hallam was advised by the video assistant referee to pause the game and consult the pitchside monitor to take a closer look at the incident.

The VAR told Hallam that Havertz was fouled by Mendy, who clearly had a hold of the striker’s jersey, but was offside at the time so the foul could not be awarded.

Upon announcing the decision to the Emirates Stadium capacity, the referee spoke of the foul by the Hull centre-back first, which caused the home faithful to cheer in delight at the penalty they thought they were being awarded.

However, their glee turned to disappointment in the blink of an eye when Hallam explained that Hull were in fact being awarded a free kick as a result of Havertz being offside.

A statement from the Premier League read: “VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty to Arsenal for a challenge by Mendy on Havertz - but determined that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up.”

Arsenal vs Hull LIVE: Latest score and updates from Premier League

Why Saliba is not in Arsenal squad against Hull despite injury return

De Zerbi issues Maddison injury update surprising Tottenham no-show

It sparked outrage amongst the Arsenal players and on the home bench, with Mikel Arteta having stern words with the fourth official on the touchline as the minutes ticked down towards the interval, where both sides went in goalless after a tense opening 45 minutes.

And it soon emerged that the penalty should have been awarded in a clear error by VAR.

BBC Sport’s football issues correspondent, Dale Johnson, reported: “That is a very controversial VAR intervention at the Emirates.

“A player who is in an offside position only becomes active when they commit an offside offence.

“Kai Havertz must be ‘attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball’ - otherwise the shirt pull by Nobel Mendy takes precedence. The foul comes before any offside offence.

“Havertz did not commit an offside offence, and this should have been a spot-kick to Arsenal regardless of the offside.

“We saw this a couple of seasons ago between Newcastle and Bournmouth. Fabian Schar was just offside but pulled back as he moved to run onto a free-kick delivery. A penalty was awarded after a VAR review.”

The IFAB ‘Laws of the Game’ for this season states: “A player in an offside position is moving towards the ball with the intention of playing the ball and is fouled before playing or attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence.”

#1805. 'Players run through brick walls for him': How Scott Parker will fix West Ham - Mark Noble's helping hand, why insiders believe he can shed defensive style... and where it all went wrong for 'distant' Nuno Espirito Santo

Published: 12:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 08:44 EDT, 4 November 2026

For a club that prides itself on playing the 'West Ham Way', it has long been impossible to decipher quite what that means these days.

Managers have come and gone with no one able to tell you what their West Ham team embodies. What was the identity under Julen Lopetegui? What was it under Graham Potter? And what, after more than a year in charge, was it under Nuno Espirito Santo? If anything, the longer it went on under Nuno, the more unclear it became.

There had long been concerns in the West Ham dressing room, and boardroom, about Nuno’s confusing tactics, unforgiving man-management and humdrum training sessions. Club insiders described him as distant.

Few can forget the time he played his full backs on the wrong side in a damaging defeat by Brentford and then sent his team out against Leeds with no recognised forward and Andy Irving in midfield.

It was little surprise to see Callum Wilson, the former Hammers striker who started on the bench in those games, liking the club’s Instagram post confirming Nuno had been sacked.

Nor to see current jettisoned midfielder Edson Alvarez do the same when he can’t get into the side despite EFL record signing Arne Engels and Divine Mukasa being overrun every week. And especially not to see the wife of goalkeeper Alphonse Areola, now playing second fiddle to Mads Hermansen, posting an Instagram story to the tune of So Long, Farewell from The Sound of Music.

There had long been concerns in the West Ham dressing room, and boardroom, about Nuno Espirito Santo’s tactics, man-management and training sessions

In Nuno's stead, West Ham have turned to former midfielder Scott Parker to get them out of the Championship

Former West Ham midfielder James Ward-Prowse, another who was bombed out under Nuno, could barely conceal his glee when asked last month after his Southampton side's win at the London Stadium whether it felt even better to get one over a manager who didn’t want you. ‘I’m not gonna lie,' he said, 'of course it does.’

Nuno’s fate is not expected to be mourned for long. West Ham’s supporters had already made their own views clear.

Spurred on by the travelling West Brom fans at the London Stadium on Saturday with their hearty rendition of ’You’re getting sacked in the morning’, the few Hammers left at the end of their 3-1 home defeat joined in.

Three days later, they got their wish. ‘Following a thorough review of the start to the Championship season, the board of directors believe a change is necessary at this time to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track,’ read the club statement.

Those expectations are to earn instant automatic promotion, considering West Ham have the most expensive squad in the division and kept hold of Jarrod Bowen after relegation. But they are eighth following those back-to-back defeats by Southampton and West Brom.

It was a surprise to many that Nuno kept his job after relegation. David Sullivan, the former majority shareholder, wanted to sack Nuno in the summer but his influence in the boardroom was fading amid the BBC Panorama expose into historic allegations about his behaviour, which he denies, that saw him stand down as joint-chair.

Daniel Kretinsky, now the man who makes the decisions, wanted to keep the ship steady but has realised a change is needed after their unimpressive start. He made the decision after a crunch meeting this week.

And, so, for their fourth permanent manager since they enjoyed European glory under David Moyes, the Hammers have turned to one of their own former players in Scott Parker, out of work since leaving Burnley in April.

Former West Ham midfielder James Ward-Prowse (centre), who was bombed out under Nuno, could barely conceal his glee after his Southampton side's win at the London Stadium

The club's expectations are to earn instant automatic promotion. But they are eighth following back-to-back defeats by Southampton and West Brom

He will be in charge for the Cardiff game on Wednesday night. They held talks with Parker in the summer and are believed to have done so again last week following the Southampton defeat.

Insiders say the club is acting with more ‘normality’ these days under the leadership of new chief executive Karim Virani, a stark change from the madcap chaos of recent years, and the appointment of Parker, a manager with a track record of getting teams promoted, feels like another step in that direction.

Parker has won three promotions with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, with the last coming after racking up 100 points in 2024-25.

And, perhaps even more importantly at a time when the club are still searching for an identity, the 46-year-old – who was named Hammer of the Year three times in a row from 2009 to 2011 – knows what it means to represent West Ham. ‘He knows the West Ham ethos,’ as one senior club source told me this morning.

It’s expected that Hammers legend Mark Noble, currently sporting director and in interim charge, will form part of Parker’s staff. The fans, at least, will have figures in the dugout they can feel connected to.

Parker’s first job will be instilling a resilience that typified his Burnley team. West Ham boast the best attack in the Championship with 33 goals, helped by pumping six past Wrexham and Lincoln, but they have the leakiest defence of any of its top 11 teams.

Eight of their 18 goals conceded have come inside the first 20 minutes and, so far this term, they have failed to win when conceding the first goal.

By contrast, Parker's sides have kept a clean sheet in nearly half of his Championship matches. Burnley kept 30 in their 2024-25 promotion campaign, conceding 16 times in 46 matches and never more than once in a game. West Ham have mustered four clean sheets in their 13 games thus far and have already let in 18.

The 46-year-old - who was named Hammer of the Year three times in a row from 2009 to 2011 - knows what it means to represent West Ham

He will get a helping hand from former team-mate Mark Noble (left), who is now sporting director

Parker is arguably the safest pair of hands West Ham could have placed their promotion hopes in. Those hoping to be freed from the turgid football of Nuno, however, may still be left disappointed.

Parker’s sides do have an identity but it’s one based firmly on being hard to beat. Those who followed Burnley under him say that if they scored even once, they knew they would likely win. ‘Dour but effective,’ was how one Burnley source put it.

Even though they ended the 2024-25 season as the third-highest scorers in the Championship, they ranked only 10th for number of shots and their expected goals (xG). Eight other teams had more touches in the opposition box.

For all the grumbles over his style, Parker’s players loved him. ‘They would run through brick walls for him,’ said one Burnley source. An unusual flurry of long, heartfelt messages from his players followed the decision to part ways.

Those players who had their noses put out of joint by Nuno have a chance to reignite their West Ham careers.

Areola won the player of the season award at Fulham after Parker brought him to the club on loan from Paris Saint-Germain. Noble previously told talkSPORT how much he ‘always respected and liked’ Alvarez as a midfielder.

There’s still a hope among senior figures that having better players at his disposal will allow Parker to play a more attractive style than during his Burnley days. Many who follow the Clarets credit him with being able to build such a resilient team after losing a host of his key players at the end of the transfer window.

The issue, of course, is what happens should Parker get West Ham back up. For all his brilliance at getting teams out of the Championship, his record at keeping them in the Premier League is equally dismal.

Alphonse Areola won the player of the season award at Fulham after Parker brought him to the club on loan from Paris Saint-Germain

Parker was sacked after just four games at Bournemouth in the 2022-23 season

Fulham and Burnley came straight back down, the latter after spending more than £100million in the summer, and he was sacked by Bournemouth just four games in after a 9-0 defeat by Liverpool and complaints his squad was ‘under-equipped’.

Parker has won 55 per cent of his matches as manager in the Championship but only 15 per cent of them in the Premier League. His points per game plummets from 1.95 in the second tier to 0.7 in the top flight.

West Ham and their supporters may well harbour reservations over how they might fare in the Premier League under Parker but, right now, are in no position to think that far ahead. They need to get there first and, more than a quarter of the way through the season, have shown little to suggest they will.

Forget the carnival of free-flowing football for now. After putting up with a circus for so long, a little sense of order might be West Ham’s way back.

#1803. Milan legend Costacurta warns Amorim’s side against complacency

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

AC Milan legend Alessandro Costacurta has warned his former side against complacency, ahead of their Serie A meeting with Genoa.

Spirits were high in Ruben Amorim's squad after they defeated rivals Inter in the league, but their momentum quickly disappeared following a 2-0 defeat against Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

The Rossoneri have 21 points after 10 games, seven fewer than early leaders Lazio heading into MD11, and they have another tough task awaiting them against Genoa.

Daniele De Rossi's side have four of their last five games in Serie A, after failing to win any of their first five this season (D1 L4).

Costacurta believes Milan's players got too ahead of themselves after defeating Inter, which led to their loss in the Europa League on Thursday.

In an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, Costacurta said: "Keeping the same intensity that they had against Inter would have been difficult.

"But at the end of the day, that’s the difference between a team that wins and one that doesn’t.

"Within four days of the 3-1 win over Inter, some of them thought they'd already become big players, and that's a serious mistake.

"Thinking you've already reached a certain height can be fatal.

"You think you can do things easily, that you will always succeed, and that's a mistake you can’t afford to make.

"[Yunus] Musah, a few minutes into the game, loses the ball cheaply. [Amadou] Diawara comes carrying the ball out from the back and then throws it away. [Alphadjo] Cisse receives the ball to feet without ever creating any trouble.

"I've framed these three, but it wasn’t all their fault. It's also clear that they didn't start with the right mentality."

Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4); since the 2020-21 season, among the teams they have never lost against in the top flight, the Rossoneri have only played more games against Hellas Verona (12).

Milan have also won their last four Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against three sides do the Rossoneri currently have a longer ongoing run of away wins in the competition: Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Martin Odegaard came to the rescue as Arsenal battled to a 1-0 win over Hull in north London.

It was a hard-fought occasion for the Gunners, who found Hull a tough nut to crack and for more than 70 minutes were kept at bay.

But Odegaard followed in after Noni Madueke’s shot was saved and that proved enough for victory, as the champions moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League for the time being.

Matt Verri was at the Emirates Stadium to rate the Arsenal players...

Not entirely convincing with one or two crosses that were put on top of him and pushed one shot straight into a dangerous area. Faced two shots on target - a busy afternoon by his standards.

Did a decent Riccardo Calafiori impression, popping up all over the pitch. Great energy and should have had an assist with perfect cross for Tzolis. Relationship with Noni Madueke still needs work, often on wrong wavelength.

Rock solid once again. Made a crucial block to deflect Mohamed Cho’s shot wide as Hull broke into the box. Made seven clearances, so often in the right place as Hull swung balls into the box.

Not quite at his imperious best. Shrugged off the ball on halfway as the visitors countered and needed Konsa to bail him out. Still enough of a presence to help Arsenal to another clean sheet and another narrow win.

One really loose moment on the ball that played Arsenal into trouble. Otherwise no real scares but does feel like his attacking threat has dipped in the last few matches. Not quite as obvious a presence going forward.

Sense that he lacked some of his usual energy. Went close from distance twice but also had some sloppy moments in possession. Little sign of his trademark driving runs. Telling he was withdrawn after an hour.

One of his better starts in an Arsenal shirt. Kept trying to force the ball between the lines and was really positive in his decision-making. Lovely combinations with Odegaard and so composed under pressure in the build-up.

Constant threat down the right in the first half. Pinpoint crosses for Konsa and Rice. More chaotic after the break, for good and bad, but he still ran Hull ragged and his shot then led to the deadlock being broken. Should have put match to bed but fluffed his lines trying to round the keeper.

Led from the front with a timely winner, following in on the rebound and converting. Had some real moments of quality before that too, sliding in Tzolis to win a dangerous free-kick and then slipping Havertz in behind. Deserved better from his attackers.

Looked sharp at Anfield but this was a big step back. Wasted two dangerous counters with poor decisions and heavy touches. Quality in the final third was sorely lacking. Improved slightly in the second half but more needed than just lots of work-rate.

#1801. Caykur Rizespor vs BB Erzurumspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:55

Caykur Rizespor will be looking to end their five-match winless run when they welcome BB Erzurumspor to Caykur Didi Stadium on Sunday, with the visitors hoping to return to winning ways after suffering a home defeat in their previous Super Lig outing.

The hosts sit 13th in the table with 11 points from 10 matches, three points behind the 11th-placed visitors, who have collected 14 points.

Rizespor's recent results have left Recep Ucar with plenty to address, as his side were held to a goalless draw by Kocaelispor last time out, although that point came after three consecutive defeats against Trabzonspor, Corum and Fenerbahce.

Their winless run began with a draw against Goztepe, marking a significant decline from their opening five league matches, during which they recorded three victories.

Their struggles at home are an even more pressing concern, with Rizespor losing all four of their matches at Caykur Didi Stadium this season, conceding 10 goals and scoring just three, leaving them as the only team in the league yet to collect a point on home soil.

They will make another attempt to change that record in what will be their first top-flight meeting with Erzurumspor since 2021, with both sides having recorded one victory each in their four previous Super Lig encounters, alongside two draws.

Erzurumspor won the most recent meeting between the teams, securing a 2-0 victory in the Turkish Cup earlier this year, and are unbeaten in their last two encounters with the hosts (W1, D1).

However, the Serkan Ozbalta's men arrive after suffering a 3-1 home defeat to Corum, which ended a four-match unbeaten run across all competitions (W3, D1).

They will be eager to bounce back immediately on the road, having recorded a positive result in their most recent away fixture, a 3-1 victory over Gaziantep that also marked their first away win of the campaign.

Erzurumspor have also won just once in four previous visits to this ground, losing twice and drawing once, suggesting that Sunday's encounter could prove difficult despite Rizespor's poor home form.

Rizespor are expected to be without Khusniddin Alikulov, who is recovering from a knee injury, while Can Bozdogan is also unavailable with an ankle problem.

Modibo Sagnan is suspended, leaving Ucar with defensive adjustments to make, while Ahmed Kutucu has also been listed as a potential absentee, although his availability remains uncertain.

Erzurumspor are likely to be without Mustafa Yumlu, who is struggling with a muscle injury, although the visitors otherwise appear to have fewer significant availability concerns.

The visitors have scored nine goals in their opening 10 league matches, with Eren Tozlu and Miguel Cardoso contributing three apiece, and both forwards will be hoping to add to their tallies as they prepare to lead the attack.

Caykur Rizespor possible starting lineup:

Gorgen; Pala, Mocsi, Bakayoko, Ariss; Diakite; Mebude, Olawoyin, Laci, Bulut; Gennaro Borrelli

Taskiran; Ovacikli, Gerxhaliu, Kirtay, Mujakic, Giorbelidze; Baiye, Owusu, Rodriguez; Cardoso, Tozlu

With neither side particularly convincing defensively, a closely contested draw looks a reasonable outcome, especially given Rizespor's difficulty turning home advantage into victories.

Erzurumspor have shown enough quality on their travels to trouble the hosts, but their own recent setback suggests they may have to settle for a point.

#1800. How Arsenal star's unforgettable performance secured champions crucial win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal huffed and puffed and eventually the Hull house came down.

A rare outing in the Saturday 3pm slot offered an opportunity. Win and the Gunners would, for a couple of hours at least, go six points clear at the top of the Premier League. Eventually, it was a chance they took full advantage of.

For much of the afternoon, that did not necessarily feel inevitable. For more than 70 minutes, Hull held firm and the champions were not exactly creating an abundance of chances.

Frustration grew around the stadium, the fear that another international break would be spent stewing with frustration and regret.

Mikel Arteta’s side had earlier in the match been denied a penalty in bizarre circumstances. Referee Farai Hallam halted play to go to the monitor, where he decided Kai Havertz had been pulled down in the box.

He returned to the pitch to announce that, sparking cheers in the stands, only those cheers drowned out the sentence that followed, stating that Havertz was offside and so the penalty would not be given.

A glance at the rules suggests that was the wrong decision and it should have been awarded regardless of the offside. When Lewie Coyle then avoided a second yellow card for hacking Christos Tzolis down early in the second half, plenty in the Emirates were fearing this might just be one of those days.

It was necessary, then, that Martin Odegaard delivered a captain’s moment, following in after Noni Madueke’s shot was saved to net the winner and drag Arsenal over the line.

The Norwegian led from the front even before the first whistle was blown. With Hull preparing to take the kick-off, Odegaard bellowed and waved frantically at Tzolis, making it clear it would be his job to close down the Hull goalkeeper when it was played back.

Early in the first half, Tzolis was getting another earful. As Odegaard led the press centrally, the ball was played out to Hull’s right into open space. The skipper sprinted back with his arms outstretched, frustrated that his winger had not been following in support.

The Arsenal captain should have had an assist before half time. He slipped a lovely ball through to Havertz who was clean through on goal, only for the German to inexplicably try and chop back onto his left foot and waste the chance.

Odegaard had a big moment at the other end of the pitch, too. When Hull broke from an Arsenal corner, it was Odegaard who found himself as the last man back.

Odegaard scores winner as Arsenal edge out Hull in nervy affair

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Mohamed Cho threatened to run in on goal and had the beating of Odegaard for pace, but the midfielder got his body in the way and won the ball back brilliantly.

After the break, the No8 provided not only the winner but the intent to keep going. He waved his team-mates on at every opportunity and buzzed around the pitch.

Only Bruno Guimaraes had more touches than Odegaard. The Norway international created five chances, more than anyone on the pitch, and he also led the way for line-breaking passes.

It was far from a convincing performance from Arsenal but that did not matter. After three away matches in a week, and with this the final game before the international break, all that mattered was a victory.

The north Londoners got that and now have nine wins from ten matches in the league. This match will be quickly forgotten, a sign that it was job done and little more than that, but Odegaard’s contribution should not be.

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:56

Fenerbahce will be looking to build on an important European victory when they travel to face Corum Belediyespor at Corum Stadyumu in the Turkish Super Lig on Sunday.

Former captain Emre Belozoglu returned to the club as head coach earlier this week, taking charge of a side sitting sixth in the table with 16 points from 10 matches, level on points with their hosts, who occupy seventh place.

Corum have made a respectable start to life in the Super Lig, winning half of their 10 league matches this season to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

After failing to win any of their opening three fixtures, the Red-Black have gone on to collect five victories in their last seven matches, with their most recent success coming in a 3-1 win away to Erzurumspor.

That victory followed their defeat to Goztepe, continuing a recent pattern in which they have responded to each of their last two league defeats with a win in their subsequent fixture.

Burak Yilmaz's side will nevertheless be aware that their defensive organisation faces a much sterner examination on Sunday, having conceded 16 goals in their opening 10 league matches, the most of any team in the top eight, although only four sides have scored more than their 21 goals.

They have scored just six of those goals at home and conceded four, while drawing two and losing two of their four matches at Corum Stadyumu this season.

Sunday's encounter will be the first meeting between the two sides, and Corum will hope to make a positive start to this new fixture, although doing so will require them to record consecutive home victories for the first time this season.

Fenerbahce, meanwhile, arrive with renewed confidence after recovering from a difficult spell to beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League, with Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi all finding the net.

That result followed consecutive 2-1 defeats against Goztepe and Galatasaray in the Super Lig, a difficult run that preceded Ismail Kartal's departure and Belozoglu's decision to leave Kasimpasa for a second spell in charge of the Yellow Canaries.

The new coach inherits a side that has produced some impressive attacking performances, with only Amed SK (25) scoring more goals than Fenerbahce (24) in the Super Lig, although their inability to turn that attacking quality into consistent victories has left them with five wins from 10 league matches and nine points behind leaders Galatasaray.

Another concern heading into Sunday's clash is their recent away form, having lost their last two competitive matches on the road and conceded in both, with their most recent setback coming against Galatasaray in the league.

Çorum Belediyespor Turkish Super Lig form:

Corum will be without Gokhan Sazdagi, who is suspended after picking up a booking in the victory over Erzurumspor.

Emircan Gurluk is also sidelined with a muscle injury, while Fredy remains a doubt after struggling with a similar problem.

Jesus Ramirez has been one of Corum's most reliable attacking players, scoring six league goals this season, and is expected to lead the line alongside Ermin Mahmic.

Fenerbahce also have several selection concerns, with Nathan Ake and Marco Asensio carrying injuries, while Jayden Oosterwolde is expected to miss out with an Achilles problem.

Archie Brown is suspended following his involvement in the post-match physical brawl against Fenerbahce, while Kojo Peprah Oppong remains a doubt.

One of Belozoglu's biggest decisions will be who leads the attack, with Romelu Lukaku competing with Muriqi, who has scored seven league goals this season and also found the net in the Champions League victory.

#1796. Leeds boss Farke defends ‘butterfly’ Bogle after ‘unlucky’ Tel challenge

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Daniel Farke insisted Jayden Bogle is the "softest player" in the Premier League, after his rash challenge on Mathys Tel went unpunished during Leeds United's 1-0 win over Tottenham.

Leeds got back to winning ways after a run of five matches without success, as Noah Okafor climbed off the bench to secure all three points at Elland Road.

However, the hosts were fortunate not to have been reduced to 10 men during the first half, when Bogle caught Tel on his Achilles with a late challenge, which forced the Spurs winger to leave the field.

Following a four-minute VAR review, Tony Harrington advised referee John Brooks not to go to his pitchside monitor, with the incident only deemed "reckless".

However, Farke jumped to the defence of the Leeds wing-back.

"I just know that Jayden Bogle never, out of any bad intention, does the foul," he told TNT Sports. "It looked a bit like an unlucky coming together – a very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured right now.

"But I know Jadon Bogle – the last thing is that he is a nasty player.

"He's normally probably the softest player in the whole league. I always call him my butterfly. Never out of bad intention, he's there with the foul – that's what I can guarantee.

"But of course, I hope that Mathys can recover pretty quickly."

Leeds also extended their unbeaten home run in the Premier League to nine matches (W5 D4), which represents their longest streak since going 15 without defeat in 2001.

And Farke was pleased to be heading into the international break with a victory.

"There's no replacement for the winning feeling after a game in the dressing room," he said. "It's important for the mood and the confidence.

"The momentum can change quickly in most directions. We've played one of the most in-form sides.

"Of course, we've had a difficult spell in the last few games. It's good to have the winning feeling back. The boys were on it, very united. Credit to my boys."

#1795. Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Martin Odegaard scores winner in tense Premier League affair

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal needed a captain’s goal from Martin Odegaard to see off Hull 1-0 and ensure they head into the international break with a healthy lead at the top of the Premier League.

Odegaard struck with 18 minutes of a tight encounter left to make it seven home wins on the spin for the champions.

The Norwegian’s fifth goal of the season also took the spotlight away from a quite bizarre VAR decision.

Play was stopped shortly before half-time for a penalty check, for a shirt-pull on Kai Havertz by Nobel Mendy.

It was nowhere near the ball, but was otherwise similar to the tug Jurrien Timber gave Liverpool’s Alexander Isak last weekend which went unpunished – only this time Havertz went down.

Referee Farai Hallam was sent to the monitor and duly announced that Mendy had indeed fouled Havertz, to a huge cheer from the home support.

However, he then added that Havertz was actually offside, and awarded a free-kick to Hull instead.

Yet Havertz was neither attempting to play the ball, nor challenging an opponent for the ball, which he would need to be in order to be deemed offside, so the laws state the foul should take precedence.

BBC pundit Dion Dublin was baffled, saying “It’s clear as mud. You’re now talking about when the ball is struck.

“They’re saying he makes the run first and he would have been offside if he hadn’t have been pulled.

“Because he’s been pulled, there’s no offside. You’re talking split seconds.”

Arsenal, who had pulled off an impressive 1-0 win at Anfield last weekend, were far from their fluent best against well-organised Hull.

They were almost caught cold inside two minutes when the Tigers won a corner which John Egan headed into the side-netting.

The hosts’ first chance came the way of centre-half Gabriel, whose glancing header from Noni Madueke’s cross flew just wide.

Arsenal should have taken the lead in the 39th minute when Timber reached the byline and cut the ball back, but Christos Tzolis blazed his first-time shot high over the top.

After the VAR fuss had died down, Arsenal went close again in first-half stoppage time, with Declan Rice heading Madueke’s cross straight at Tzolakis.

After the break Hull keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis kept out Madueke’s shot with his legs and held a curler from Greece team-mate Tzolis.

The breakthrough arrived in the 72nd minute when Tzolakis could only parry Madueke’s drive and Odegaard reacted quickest to tuck in the rebound.

The Gunners almost had a second when Madueke rounded Tzolakis and the ball rolled towards goal, but Brooke Norton-Cuffy cleared from under the crossbar.

#1794. Alanyaspor vs Trabzonspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:56

Alanyaspor will be looking to halt a worrying run of results when they welcome Trabzonspor to Alanya Oba Stadium on Sunday, while the visitors have an opportunity to strengthen their position near the top of the Turkish Super Lig table.

The hosts sit 12th with 12 points from 10 matches, whereas the Black Sea Storm occupy third place on 22 points after winning seven of their opening 10 league fixtures.

Alanyaspor suffered a 5-0 defeat away to Genclerbirligi last time out, extending their losing run to three consecutive league matches following earlier setbacks against Kocaelispor and Fenerbahce.

They have conceded 10 goals across those three matches, a significant decline from their previous four-game unbeaten run, during which they recorded two victories and two draws while conceding just three goals.

Their only positive result in recent weeks came in the Turkish Cup, where they beat Bingol 4-1 to end a three-match winless run on home soil.

However, Joao Pereira's side are without a victory in their last three league matches at Alanya Oba Stadium, drawing twice and losing their most recent game against Kocaelispor, with their only home league victory this season coming against Besiktas.

Alanyaspor will hope to show greater resilience on Sunday, particularly given their recent record in this fixture, having remained unbeaten in their last three competitive meetings with Trabzonspor, recording one win and two draws.

Their home record against the visitors is even more impressive, with the hosts unbeaten in their last four matches at Alanya Oba Stadium (W3, D1), while they have lost just twice in their last 10 home meetings, winning five and drawing three.

Trabzonspor, meanwhile, arrive in impressive domestic form, with no side collecting more points than them across the last five league matches, having maintained a perfect record during that period.

They recorded a 2-0 victory over Gaziantep in their most recent league outing, extending a winning run that also includes victories over Caykur Rizespor, Besiktas, Samsunspor and Galatasaray.

That five-match league winning streak formed part of a seven-game run of victories across all competitions, but their momentum was halted on Thursday when the Black Sea Storm suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League.

Thomas Reis will hope that setback proves to be only a minor distraction as his side look to maintain their domestic form and close the three-point gap to league leaders Galatasaray.

They can also take encouragement from their recent performances away from home, having recorded three consecutive victories on the road across all competitions, a significant improvement after failing to win any of their first four away matches of the season.

Alanyaspor are expected to be without Paolo Fernandes, who has been struggling with a muscle injury, while defender Fatih Aksoy is also a doubt after missing the defeat to Genclerbirligi.

Their potential absences would be a concern for Pereira, particularly after his side conceded five goals in Ankara, where Bedirhan Ozyurt replaced Aksoy in the back three.

Gaius Makouta, Maestro and Baran Gezek are expected to feature in midfield, while Ruan and Florent Hadergjonaj should occupy the wing-back positions.

Trabzonspor have a longer list of potential absentees, with Arseniy Batagov, Ruslan Malinovskyi, Okay Yokuslu and Aral Simsir all listed among the players who could miss out.

Cihan Canak and Franculino are further concerns for Reis, while Sidny Lopes Cabral is available again after missing the European fixture through suspension.

Ernest Muci leads the Super Lig assist charts with six this season and will be looking to create further opportunities for Mohamed Salah, who has scored eight league goals, one fewer than joint-top scorers Victor Osimhen and Gift Orban.

Victor; Lima, Ozyurt, Aliti; Hadergjonaj, Makouta, Gezek, Maestro, Ruan; Kaya, Cedric

#1793. Homicide police launch investigation into on-pitch collision that killed Spanish footballer - after goalkeeper clashed with fans shouting 'murderer' at him

Published: 07:31 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 09:51 EDT, 4 November 2026

Police have launched a homicide investigation into the on-pitch collision that led to the death of a Spanish footballer.

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, 30, died this morning just hours after receiving a flying knee to the chest from Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off before the match in Spain's second division was abandoned.

Owono, 25, is reportedly planning to apologise to de Miguel's family. He is said to be 'deeply upset' and has insisted there was 'no intention to cause harm'.

The Andorra goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by the Tenerife fans, who clashed with him as he left the pitch.

And the Homicide Group of the National Police in Santa Cruz de Tenerife are now investigating what happened during the match.

But other reports suggest Owono is expected to avoid criminal sanctions over the horrifying on-pitch collision, with his challenge likely to only result in sporting penalties.

In Spain, investigations are typically opened for any deaths not linked to natural causes.

Spanish sports lawyer Miguel Galan said today: 'The Supreme Court's doctrine states that excesses during a play are subject to sporting, not criminal, sanctions.'

Tenerife, from Spain's second tier of football, confirmed Jesus de ​Miguel's death in a statement this morning

Goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono has reportedly insisted there was 'no intention to cause harm' after his challenge led to the death of the Tenerife striker

De Miguel was admitted to intensive care after the tackle. However, Tenerife announced today that his condition had worsened overnight and he passed away this morning after entering cardiac arrest.

The striker was treated for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

Journalist Iván Alvarez, speaking on COPE radio before De Miguel's death was announced, reported that the goalkeeper intended to apologise to De Miguel's family in person.

Alvarez added that Owono and Andorra FC had insisted there had been 'no intention to cause harm' and that the goalkeeper had closed his Instagram account after being subjected to 'murderer' chants and messages.

'Some of the people who were at the stadium and some messages I exchanged with players told me it's the hardest thing they've ever experienced on a football pitch,' the journalist said.

He added that Owono is 'very upset' and that 'no one would ever think of someone wanting to harm a fellow professional in that way'.

Alvarez continued: 'Andorra emphasises that there was no ill intent at any point, acknowledging that it was a mistimed outburst, an action that went terribly wrong and, I would say, excessive and violent, but they insist there was no intention to cause harm.

'Owono, who doesn't appreciate hearing an entire stadium like the Heliodoro chanting "murderer, murderer", has even closed his Instagram account after all the criticism he's received this afternoon.

'His intention is to contact Jesus de Miguel's family or someone close to him personally, when the time is right. He wants to do so privately first, before making any public statement.'

Footage taken from the stands had shown Owono clashing with supporters as he left the pitch.

The AS newspaper reported that a challenge judged to be an act of 'violent conduct toward an opponent during a game that causes serious injury or harm' is punishable by a suspension of four to 12 games.

Owono is reportedly intending to apologise directly to de Miguel's family for his challenge and has made his social media private following abusive chants and messages he received (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

Mientras se llevaban a De Miguel inconsciente y en parada cardiorrespiratoria, Owono se marchaba a vestuarios encarándose con la grada. No está bien de la cabeza.Vídeo de autoría desconocida. pic.twitter.com/41LxJnVuaF

Owono is a current Equatorial Guinea international and has represented his nation 44 times, including playing at the Africa Cup of Nations twice.

He grew up in the Basque Country after moving to San Sebastian in northern Spain at the age of eight.

Owono came through Real Sociedad's youth academy and joined Alaves at 16.

He became the first player born in Equatorial Guinea to play in the Spanish top flight.

Owono played 11 LaLiga matches before joining Andorra on loan last season and signed permanently for the club this summer.

The goalkeeper and his team-mates had reportedly returned to Barcelona this morning.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Rayco Garcia, Tenerife's majority shareholder, and the club's president Felipe Minambres spoke of their 'unbearable pain' after de Miguel's death.

The club confirmed plans for fans to pay tribute to the striker this Saturday at their stadium, while outlining that his team-mates will receive support following the tragedy.

Rayco said on Radio Marca Tenerife: 'We are facing an unprecedented situation. We are very hurt, Tenerife fans are in mourning. It is very difficult to accept. Tomorrow, or the day after tomorrow, we will have the definitive "ok" to transfer the player's body, at the express wish of his family, to Navahermosa, in Toledo.

'There we will pay our last farewell to Jesús de Miguel. On Saturday we summoned all the fans of the island, at 18:00, at the Heliodoro, to say our last goodbye together, and we will join forces to move forward. Life has hit us all, but we are a big family and we are going to move forward.'

Minambres added: 'It is a very sad day... It is an unlived situation, that a player dies like this on a pitch. We are in moments of weakness, of sadness, of not believing what has happened.

'We will go through the mourning and this will make us more united. We have to spend a week in mourning, we are going to need professional help, us, the players and their families. Also that of our followers.

'We have to pay the tribute that "Demi" deserves. We will always carry it in our hearts. It is a great misfortune that we have suffered.'

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

In a statement this morning, CD Tenerife had confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.

'There are no words of comfort. There is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

De Miguel had become a father just last year and, according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands at the time of the fatal collision.

Tributes have been paid to the striker from across the football world following the tragic incident.

European football body Uefa has confirmed that a minute of silence will be held at all their matches this week in tribute to De Miguel. Arsenal held a minute of silence at training this morning.

Uefa president Aleksander Čeferin said: 'We are heartbroken by the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.

'We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss.'

De Miguel was stretchered off the field following the collision with Owono

The Royal Spanish Football Federation have meanwhile cancelled all domestic matches today.

Tenerife's opponents Andorra offered their condolences following news of De Miguel's death, writing: 'With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.'

Football clubs across Spain, including Barcelona and Real Madrid, have led tributes following the news of the death.

'Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times,' Barcelona said in a statement.

Real Madrid also expressed their condolences, stating: 'Real Madrid wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club, and all his loved ones.'

The Spanish Footballers Association also released a statement, expressing its 'deepest sorrow' at the footballer's death.

It read: 'His loss leaves a huge void among those of us who shared his passion for football, his commitment to the footballers' community, and his work defending the rights of our fellow professionals.

'The Board of Directors, all the staff of AFE, and the footballers' community wish to extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to his teammates at Club Deportivo Tenerife. In these moments of immense sadness, we send them all our love, support, and solidarity. You will always be part of our family.'

De Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 30 appearances to help secure the team promotion from the Spanish third division as champions.

The forward had previously helped to secure Internacional de Madrid and CD Castellón promotions from the fourth and third divisions, respectively.

CD Castellon also released a statement on Tuesday morning in tribute to their former player, saying: 'With broken hearts and inconsolable grief, Club Deportivo Castellón bids farewell to Jesus De Miguel.

'Words fail to express the profound injustice of this loss. He wore this shirt with pride, celebrated goals with our fans at the SkyFi Castalia stadium, and was an integral part of a story that this fanbase will never forget.

'We extend our deepest condolences to his family and loved ones, offering them our heartfelt support during this difficult time. We also join CD Tenerife and its fans in mourning, sharing this sorrow with them. You will always be one of us, Demi. Rest in peace.'

#1791. Fulham 1-1 Newcastle: Rodrigo Muniz salvages point but Alvaro Arbeloa sweating over injury concern

Jacob Murphy’s wonderful late strike was not enough to earn Newcastle victory at Craven Cottage, with Rodrigo Muniz levelling minutes later to earn Fulham a deserved 1-1 draw.

For 79 minutes here, there was almost nothing to stop supporters of Newcastle fearing a slide towards mid-table mediocrity. Then came Murphy’s rocket.

There was no apparent threat when the midfielder picked up the ball just inside Fulham’s half and saw little on in front of him.

All game, visiting fans had craved someone to take responsibility for their team’s blunted attack, and here it was, a brilliant, curling drive into the far corner seemingly to win it.

Alvaro Arbeloa had sent on Muniz in the 65th minute in search of the winning goal. Instead he was on hand to poach the equaliser, taking advantage of a mess in Newcastle’s penalty area to earn a point. It was the least Fulham’s display had warranted.

Only an outrageous save in stoppage time from Lukas Hornicek kept Matthias Jaissle from witnessing his team lose for the fifth time this season, Ryan Sessegnon the player denied a stunning goal from range.

Fulham, finding their feet under Arbeloa, were comfortably the better side. Early on, Dan Burn missed his clearance and the ball ran through to Oscar Bobb who drew a two-handed save from Hornicek. From the corner, Gonzalo Garcia’s header landed on top of the bar.

Newcastle’s approach was that of a team that had conceded four goals in two of their last three away matches, a cautious low block that squeezed Fulham’s room to play but which also limited their own threat to the occasional break.

Bernd Leno saved with his foot from Harvey Barnes’ clever flick at the end of one such foray forward, then the Newcastle winger was denied again by the goalkeeper after catching out Fulham’s high defensive line.

Burn prodded the ball into the net from the corner that followed but was denied for a foul given against Yoane Wissa, to the visible frustration of Jaissle.

Josh King almost celebrated his England call-up by scoring the goal of his young life, Hornicek on hand to beat away a fizzing volley from 20 yards. The 19-year-old ought still to have sent Fulham in ahead at the break, heading Alex Iwobi’s cross wide unmarked in stoppage time.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Joshua Kimmich expressed his delight at "special" team-mate Harry Kane committing his future to Bayern Munich, following Saturday's victory over Mainz.

The recently crowned Ballon d'Or winner ended speculation surrounding his future earlier this week, by penning a new deal with the Bundesliga champions until 2029.

Kane celebrated his latest landmark by creating further Bundesliga history in the 2-1 win over Mainz, during which he set up both goals.

That took his assist tally for the season to eight already, which is the highest by any player after the opening nine matchdays of a German top-flight campaign.

And Kimmich, who opened the scoring at the MEWA Arena, paid tribute to the England captain.

#1789. Besiktas vs Genclerbirligi - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:57, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:53

Besiktas will look to return to winning ways when they welcome Genclerbirligi to Tupras Stadium on Sunday in the Turkish Super Lig.

The Black Eagles sit fourth in the standings with 19 points from their opening 10 matches, while the visitors occupy 14th place with 11 points after an inconsistent start to their return to the top flight.

Besiktas have made a reasonably encouraging start to the campaign but will be frustrated by their inability to maintain consistency, having collected just seven points from their last five league matches (W2, D1, L2).

Vincenzo Italiano's side were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa in their most recent league outing, despite taking the lead twice, following a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir that had provided a timely response to their 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

They have also struggled to find consistent success in Europe, drawing 2-2 with Crystal Palace before suffering a disappointing 3-2 defeat away to Celtic in the Europa League on Thursday, leaving them with just one win from their three matches in the competition, a 3-2 victory over Hoffenheim.

Nevertheless, their home form should provide encouragement heading into this clash, having won all five of their league matches at Tupras Stadium this season and remained unbeaten there across all competitions.

However, the hosts will be hoping to buck the recent trend in this fixture, with the away side winning each of the last five competitive meetings between the teams.

Genclerbirligi, meanwhile, head to Istanbul with renewed confidence after producing one of their best performances of the season in a 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor.

Bernd Storck's side ended a seven-game winless run in the league with that result (D2, L5), which also followed a 5-0 victory over Karakopru in the Turkish Cup, giving them momentum ahead of Sunday's encounter.

The visitors will hope to carry that confidence into their next away fixture as they look to end a three-game losing run on the road, during which they have conceded 11 goals without scoring.

Their only away victory and goal of the campaign coming against Goztepe (1-0) in their opening trip, with no side scoring fewer than them on the road in this campaign.

Besiktas are expected to remain without Fabio Miretti, who is sidelined with a shoulder problem, while Umit Akdag is also set to miss out with a broken wrist and Milot Rashica continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.

Dusan Vlahovic should lead the attack after scoring seven league goals this season, with Leandro Trossard and Vaclav Cerny likely to provide support in the final third.

Orkun Kokcu returned from injury against Celtic and marked his comeback with a goal, putting himself in contention to start in midfield alongside Junior Olaitan and Salih Ozcan.

Genclerbirligi also have several availability concerns, with Dimitrios Goutas facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a cruciate ligament injury.

Pedro Pereira and Kevin Rodrigues are also carrying fitness problems, while Peter Etebo remains a doubt with a muscle injury.

Franco Tongya will be one to watch for the visitors after scoring twice in the league this season, while Tiago Gouveia and Adama Traore are expected to provide attacking support after featuring in the 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor.

Nubel; Murillo, Agbadou, Topcu, Ouattara; Ozcan; Cerny, Kokcu, Olaitan, Trossard; Vlahovic

Egribayat; Celik, Baltaci, Thalisson, Aydar; Niasse; Gouveia, Ulgun, Tongya, Traore; Mendes

Genclerbirligi's recent victories mean they should arrive in Istanbul with renewed confidence, but reproducing their attacking performance against Besiktas will be considerably more difficult.

The visitors' poor away record is another concern, and we expect the hosts to have too much quality at Tupras Stadium as they return to winning ways with a comfortable victory.

#1788. Mikel Arteta responds to Arsenal penalty decision amid VAR controversy against Hull

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta admitted he was surprised that Arsenal were not awarded a penalty in the win over Hull, as he called for “clarity” on the offside laws.

Martin Odegaard struck the only goal of the match with 20 minutes remaining to drag the Gunners past their stubborn opponents.

That came after there was controversy in the first half over a potential penalty decision.

The referee halted play to go to the monitor and review replays of Kai Havertz being dragged back in the box.

Farai Hallam announced that was a foul, but a penalty was not given as Havertz was offside.

However, the rules are ambiguous on such incidents. One interpretation is that as Havertz was not “attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball,” he was not committing an offside offence.

That would mean a penalty should have been given but the law is complicated and there are examples in the past of it being interpreted in different ways.

Arsenal have been caught offside 35 times this season, by far the most in the Premier League, but Arteta jokingly referred to the penalty decision when that stat was put to him in his post-match press conference.

He said: “Are you counting the penalty? So 34!”

Pressed for his opinion on the Havertz incident, Arteta continued: “I don’t know, I haven’t watched it back.

“I didn’t watch it back so I don’t have to lie to you guys. I was surprised, because when they sent the referee to the monitor the bench was telling me that it’s a clear penalty, it’s pulling.

“I know they decided not to because the starting position of Kai was offside, so I don’t know what the interpretation is. I’m sure they will make that clear to understand it.”

Last season, Brentford were awarded a penalty against Leeds, though that was ruled out by VAR due to a Brentford player being offside.

“I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making,” Arteta said when asked if the laws were too complicated.

He added: “We don’t have any clarity yet about the decision.”
