#1753. Man United conjured a miraculous comeback against Roma that was thrilling, visceral and raw... finally Michael Carrick has something to cling to, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 17:15 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:17 EDT, 4 November 2026

Once again they sang Michael Carrick's name and this time it was not out of sympathy. This time it was different.

This time there had been some guts and this time there had been some glory. This time, most importantly, there had been a victory. So the Stretford End sang Carrick's name out of thanks. Finally some respite from the relentless misery of this tortuous season.

How Carrick's Manchester United team pulled off this comeback is hard to fathom. But for now all that matters to Carrick is that they did. For at last he has something tangible to cling to as he tries to drag his club's season back from the jaws of hell.

How on earth do we describe this game? Maybe just with the facts.

Carrick's team were so bad in the first half it was almost impossible to understand. However awful they have been this season, this was worse. Two down to early goals from Matias Soule and Donyell Malen, United presented both to Roma on a plate.

The game looked over. United's Champions League season looked over. Carrick's reign felt over.

Matheus Cunha's late double rescued Manchester United from the jaws of defeat on a night of madness at Old Trafford

Cunha scored in the 83rd and 86th minute to turn the game on its head against Roma

There was still time for Cunha to be sent off in the dying embers of the game - but that failed to take the shine off a memorable night

In the crowd they waved green and gold balloons in protest at the owners the Glazers. Then they threw tennis balls on to the field. The only surprise was that none of the United players put one in their own net.

But then, somehow and almost impossibly, this game changed. Whether it will be enough to prompt a genuine shift in the course of United's season, only time will tell. The chances are it won't. There is too much wrong.

They were lucky to be given an early second-half penalty and lucky that Bruno Fernandes was given the chance to take it again after he missed the first one. They were then lucky in the 83rd minute when Matheus Cunha was handed an equaliser by a defensive howler.

But luck is no good if you don't ride it. And the winning goal Cunha delivered into the net at the near post with four minutes left was not about luck. It was about a team and a player seizing the opportunity to write a different story.

It was born of desire, desperation and perhaps some anger after the pain of the last few weeks. Within a second, the Brazilian's shirt was off and he was in the crowd.

It was hard to blame Cunha, even if he was to pay a price. Booked for that, he was soon cautioned again for a foul and was forced to leave the scene early. At least it was to an ovation. We have not heard one of those here for a while.

Old Trafford was jumping. Of course it was. Thus far this season has brought United supporters only embarrassment and at times earlier here this had felt like a new low. The way United played in the first half was arguably worse than anything we saw under Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

Matias Soule had given Roma the lead after only 11 minutes

The game was briefly halted in the first-half when fans threw objects including tennis balls onto the pitch

United boss Michael Carrick suffered a further blow when Carlos Baleba limped off

United were in full self-harm mode and in truth could have been four down by half-time.

There was actually nothing in this game for the first 10 minutes but United hurtled from safety to dire straits in the space of seven minutes. That's the way it tends to go and the first Roma goal was simply extraordinary.

When United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo lost the ball in his own half, his team found themselves a defender short. Diogo Dalot, the left back, was so far up field he may as well have been on the Stretford End.

When Rodrigo Mora switched the ball across into the space where Dalot should have been, Soule had time to cut inside and shoot low in to Senne Lammens' bottom left hand corner.

It was one of those goals that looked stranger the more you studied it. Six minutes later, United presented Roma with another one.

Once again Dalot was out of position as the ball reached goalscorer Soule on the edge of the penalty area. This time only a sliding block from Leny Yoro denied the Argentine his second goal but the ball had struck the defender's raised arm and former Aston Villa forward Malen slid in the penalty.

United were shambolic. Fernandes was booked for being, well, Fernandes. It was a harsh card but sadly the United captain's reputation now precedes him. It's the way it works in sport.

As half-time neared, Malen brought a low save from Lammens before Soule curled one from 18 yards that must have missed the righthand post by no more than six inches.

That was the difference between United being out of the game and still in with the chance of the kind of comeback they eventually produced.

Cunha was desperately fortunate to be awarded the penalty that started it all just before the hour. He seemed to trip himself up. Fernandes was then lucky to be offered a retake after his first kick was saved. The level of encroachment by a Roma defender didn't seem to meet the threshold written in law.

But once Fernandes smashed the retake high into the net Roma suddenly found themselves facing a different home team and a different environment.

Bruno Fernandes' first penalty was saved - but he made amends with his second after the referee ordered a retake for encroachment

Victory eases the pressure on United boss Michael Carrick

Carrick will perhaps argue he deserves some fortune. He certainly didn't get any as his team lost at Chelsea at the weekend. Nevertheless, his team needed some more.

Bryan Mbeumo had struck both posts with one shot after running clear immediately after Fernandes' goal while a header from Harry Maguire at a corner hit an opponent when it appeared to be heading in.

But United's fire seemed to be on the verge of burning out when a harmless 83rd-minute cross from Fernandes was completely missed by Roma defender Leonardo Balerdi to present Cunha with an equaliser from six yards.

Roma were by now a shell of the team that they had been in the first half. They had been knocked from their feet by a red tidal wave, and when Cunha unleashed a hammer shot from an angle three minutes later they were dead.

#1752. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1751. Barry-Murphy revels in ‘memorable’ Cardiff comeback against Burnley

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Brian Barry-Murphy lauded his Cardiff City players for their "memorable" comeback against Burnley, having fought back from 4-1 down to stun the Clarets with a 5-4 win.

Burnley, who had won just two of their previous 43 league games ahead of their trip to the Cardiff City Stadium, found themselves two goals to the good within 25 minutes.

Andreas Hountondji and Marcus Edwards put the Clarets in a commanding position, but Ollie Tanner pulled one back for the hosts five minutes before the break.

However, Fabio Celestini's side pulled further ahead with two more goals, with Largie Ramazani's strike followed up by an own goal from Alex Robertson just after the hour.

Yousef Salech made an instant impact off the bench to pull one back for Cardiff, and they got within one of their opponents through Jack Moylan's 75th-minute penalty.

Salech scored his second eight minutes from time to level things up, and the sensational comeback was completed by Robertson, who atoned for his earlier error with a 94th-minute strike that beat Gregoire Coudert and picked out the top-right corner.

"It's a very memorable day," Barry-Murphy said. "Even at 4-1 we felt we could be dangerous, but we obviously knew of the consequences if we didn't.

"We had a lot of players playing who normally wouldn't have played. Perry [Ng] was playing with one leg, Kristian Bielik wasn't fit, Will Fish and Alex Robertson the same.

"It felt like a throwback to days gone by in that sense.

"From the moment we got the second goal, I felt as though we had become a very dangerous team, and the players' belief was very evident.

"We have a very small squad that is stretched very thin, but we still have lots of attacking players who are so willing to learn and improve."

Never. Give. Up. #CityAsOne https://t.co/mnnhyirHRy

— Cardiff City FC (@CardiffCityFC) November 7, 2026

It was a game filled with drama, with Cardiff racking up an expected goals total of 4.65 from 25 attempts, compared to Burnley's tally of 2.3 xG from 15 shots at goal.

Cardiff ensured they did not lose back-to-back league games against Burnley for the first time since April 1977, but it was yet more misery for the Clarets.

Burnley remain inside the relegation zone on 10 points, level with Derby County, who ended their own winless league run with a 3-1 win over Bolton Wanderers on Friday.

Celestini, however, was bemused by the lack of fight and endeavour from his players, adding that squandering a three-goal lead showed the fragility within his squad.

"When it is 4-1, you have to control the game. We have to talk about what went wrong, live, it is very difficult to understand because you are emotional," Celestini conceded.

"Maybe we have to understand where we are and what our situation is. I can understand if there is fragility at 1-0, but it cannot happen at 4-1.

"It's very difficult to accept the situation, but in the last two games the team was more consistent.

"Normally, you don't need to score four or five times to win a game, but that's the reality."

#1750. Vitoria de Guimaraes vs Porto - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 06 Nov 2026 21:01, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 22:54

Porto will be looking to maintain their perfect Liga Portugal record when they travel to the Estadio D. Afonso Henriques on Sunday to face a Vitoria de Guimaraes side hoping to build on their recent defensive improvement.

Francesco Farioli's men have collected all 30 points available from their opening 10 matches, putting them five points clear at the top of the Primeira Liga table, while the Conquerors sit 13th with nine points.

Ending a four-year wait for the Primeira Liga title last season was an impressive achievement for Farioli in his first campaign in charge, but Porto have raised the bar further this term by making their best start to a league season since 1939-40.

The Dragons have won all 10 of their opening top-flight fixtures, although they still have some way to go before matching their club record of 13 consecutive victories, set during that historic 1939-40 campaign.

Farioli's side have been equally impressive at both ends of the pitch, with only Benfica (27) scoring more than their tally of 25 in the division, while their four goals conceded represent the league's best defensive record, alongside a joint-high six clean sheets.

Porto head to Guimaraes in confident mood after following up a 4-0 league victory over Estoril Praia with an emphatic 4-1 Champions League triumph over Napoli on Wednesday, extending their winning streak to four matches across all competitions.

The visitors will also take encouragement from their recent record at this venue, having won each of their last eight competitive meetings with Vitoria at the Estadio D. Afonso Henriques and kept clean sheets in their most recent three visits.

Vitoria, however, can draw some encouragement from their improved defensive displays, having gone three consecutive competitive matches without conceding since Lucas Furtado took over between the posts.

After managing just one victory in their opening eight league fixtures and enduring a five-match winless run, the Conquerors edged lower-league Lamelas in the Taca de Portugal before following up a 5-0 thrashing of Maritimo with a goalless draw against fellow Minho outfit Gil Vicente last weekend.

That stalemate in Barcelos leaves Vitoria with two wins, three draws and five defeats from their opening 10 league matches, although it did provide their first away point of the campaign after four consecutive top-flight defeats on the road.

The Guimaraes outfit have been considerably more productive on home soil, collecting eight of their nine league points at the Estadio D. Afonso Henriques, and will hope that familiar surroundings can help them frustrate the league leaders.

There is still plenty of room for improvement in attack, however, as Vitoria have scored just 10 goals in the Primeira Liga this season, with only Gil Vicente (eight) and Maritimo (nine) managing fewer among teams outside the relegation playoff places, although the Conqueror’s defensive record has been more respectable at 10 conceded.

Vitoria de Guimaraes form (all competitions):

Vitoria remain without goalkeeper Juan Castillo, who is recovering from an ankle sprain, and left-back Francisco Dias, who continues to recover from a foot ligament injury.

Thiago Balieiro is also a doubt after missing the draw with Gil Vicente due to a knee complaint, potentially leaving Margarido with the same central defensive partnership of Toni Borevkovic and Ahmed Sidibe.

Furtado is expected to retain his place between the posts after overseeing three consecutive clean sheets, while Arnel Jakupovic could lead the attack again as he looks to add to his two league goals this term.

Porto are expected to be without Chris Smalling (knee) and Vasco Sousa, while William Gomes remains sidelined with a broken ankle.

Zaidu Sanusi could return to contention after resuming unrestricted training earlier this week, while Oskar Pietuszewski's inclusion on the bench against Napoli as an unused substitute suggests that he is nearing full fitness.

Gabri Veiga and Borja Sainz have both scored five league goals this season, although the former heads into Sunday's encounter in particularly good form after netting and providing an assist in each of his last two appearances.

Samu Aghehowa also came off the bench to convert a penalty against Napoli, although it remains to be seen whether the Spaniard will displace Andre Silva in the starting lineup.

#1748. Rio Ave vs Braga - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 06 Nov 2026 21:21

Braga will be looking to secure back-to-back league victories for the second time this season when they travel to Vila do Conde on Sunday to face a struggling Rio Ave side.

An emphatic win over Famalicao on November 1 lifted Franclim Carvalho's men to eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 14 points from 10 matches, while the hosts have managed just two league victories and currently sit 16th.

Despite finishing in the top four last season, Braga missed out on a Europa League place after second-tier Torreense secured the spot by stunning Sporting Lisbon in the Taca de Portugal final, meaning the Archbishops would have entered this campaign targeting a return to the top three and more secure continental qualification.

However, the Arsenalists find themselves six points behind fifth-placed Arouca after winning just four of their opening 10 league fixtures (D2, L4), although they ended a three-match losing run in the Primeira Liga with a commanding 3-0 victory over Famalicao last weekend.

That result offered some measure of revenge after Braga suffered a penalty shootout defeat to the same Minho rivals in the Taca da Liga four days earlier, while also giving Carvalho his first top-flight win since succeeding the sacked Carlos Vicens in mid-October.

Carvalho, whose first victory in charge came against Gent in the Conference League, also guided his side to a goalless draw away to Aarhus in midweek, meaning the Arsenalists have now gone two consecutive matches across all competitions without conceding.

However, there is still room for improvement in attack, particularly after Braga failed to score in Denmark despite registering 26 shots, including nine on target, while only Gil Vicente (eight) have scored fewer than the Archbishops' 12 league goals among teams currently in the top 12.

The Arsenalists’ attacking shortcomings have been particularly evident away from home, where they have drawn a blank in each of their last five matches across all competitions and gone without a victory in that period, losing three times, including a 1-0 defeat to Nacional on their most recent league trip.

Rio Ave, meanwhile, have struggled to find consistency since Vasco Seabra took charge, winning once and losing twice in his three league matches after replacing Sotiris Silaidopoulos in October.

Seabra began his tenure with a 3-2 top-flight win over Nacional, but despite beating lower-league Louletano in the Taca de Portugal, his side suffered a 4-0 league defeat to Famalicao before losing 2-1 to Academico de Viseu last weekend, despite Miguel Patricio opening the scoring.

Defensive problems have been a recurring theme for the Vila do Conde outfit, who have conceded a league-high 23 goals this season, at least four more than any other side in the division, while their attack has offered little relief after finding the net just nine times.

The Vilacondenses' defensive frailties have been particularly apparent on home soil, where they have conceded multiple goals in each of their five league matches this term, recording just one win and a draw alongside three losses.

Rio Ave can, however, take some encouragement from their recent home meetings with Braga, having avoided defeat in each of the last three, including a 2-1 victory when the sides last met in Vila do Conde in March 2025, while their most recent encounter at the venue ended in a 2-2 draw in August 2025.

Rio Ave goalkeeper Cezary Miszta (back) and defender Nelson Abbey remain unavailable, while Pedro Amaral is a doubt after missing each of the last three league outings.

Enner Van der Gouw was preferred to Vitor Hugo between the posts last time out and could retain his place, while Patricio is also expected to feature again after getting on the scoresheet in that encounter.

Andre Ntoi picked up a red card in stoppage time last time out and is expected to serve a suspension, leaving him unavailable for Sunday's contest.

Braga are expected to remain without Sikou Niakate, who is working his way back from a lengthy Achilles tendon injury that has kept him sidelined since April.

Gabriel Silva is also a doubt after missing the last three matches, although Bright Arrey-Mbi appears to have returned to full fitness after making a brief appearance in the midweek match against Aarhus.

Van der Gouw; Tome, Pertasso, Mancha, Vrousai; Nascimento, Liavas; Clemmensen, Patricio, Bezerra; Blesa

Bernardo; Gomez, Lagerbielke, Barcia, Travassos; Gorby, Dorgeles, Moutinho; G Martinez, P Victor, Horta

Rio Ave's defensive record makes it difficult to see them keeping a resurgent Braga attack at bay, and although the visitors have struggled for goals on their travels, their commanding display against Famalicao suggests they could have enough to edge Sunday's contest.

#1747. Madueke has been a different player since England snub, says Arteta

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Noni Madueke has been a completely different player since being left out of the England squad earlier this season, believes Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

The Gunners hold a six-point advantage over Manchester City at the top of the Premier League going into the international break, after battling to a 1-0 win over Hull City.

Martin Odegaard scored the only goal of Saturday's game, pouncing to slot home after Konstantinos Tzolakis could only parry Madueke's strike in the 72nd minute.

Madueke, who continues to deputise for the injured Bukayo Saka, was Arsenal's most prominent threat during what was a frustrating game for the most part, recording match-high figures for shots (four), expected goals (0.37 xG), touches in the box (14), dribbles attempted (eight) and completed (six) and duels won (eight).

Only Odegaard, meanwhile, bettered Madueke's four chances created, with the Norwegian laying on five.

And Arteta believes Madueke has reached a new level since the previous international break, when he was omitted from Thomas Tuchel's England squad despite being a regular contributor at this year's World Cup.

Madueke has again been overlooked for the November Nations League fixtures, but when reflecting on the way the winger went away to train on his own during the last hiatus, Arteta said his reaction has been exemplary.

Arteta said of the winger: "The way he reacted to that, I think, is a great example for the rest of the squad, which is, 'I want to do more.'

"He went away, he started to train and was a different Noni. He wasn't going to accept that situation, he meant business. Since then, he has been incredible.

"He knew he had three clear chances to score. He contributed and impacted in the action for the goal for Martin, but there are still margins we can work on, to make him more efficient."

Good to be home  See you after the international break  https://t.co/bCORHnNefQ

Saturday's win was Arsenal's 34th by a 1-0 scoreline under Arteta in the Premier League, the most of any club since the Spaniard took the reins in December 2019.

And Arteta knows the Gunners can be better in the final third, citing their high number of offsides – including one against Kai Havertz that cost them a penalty in the first half – as something they must work on.

"We need to be more efficient. We were one-on-one with the 'keeper twice, and maybe there was a penalty there too," Arteta said.

"There were shots deflected, blocked… we need to insist, to find ways to be more efficient and pragmatic.

"Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

"There are many areas we need to improve, and one of them is the offsides – they are sometimes related to the timing of the situations, where you line up and what space is given to you.

"There have been too many, the Villa game puts those stats in a different perspective – the sample is quite short still to analyse it properly – but that is a point."

Arsenal return to action against Newcastle United on November 21, at St James' Park, before hosting Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League and facing Manchester City in a titanic tussle between the Premier League's top two.

#1746. Santa Clara vs Gil Vicente - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 06 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 21:32

Santa Clara will be looking to strengthen their position in the upper echelons of the Primeira Liga table and move within one point of second-placed Benfica when they take on Gil Vicente on Sunday.

The Gilistas have also made an encouraging start to the campaign, but they journey to the Estadio de Sao Miguel aiming to arrest their recent dip and secure a third consecutive away victory in the league.

Santa Clara turned in a comprehensive team display to return to winning ways last Sunday as they edged out Maritimo 2-0 when the two sides squared off at the Estadio do Maritimo.

While Maritimo squandered several clear-cut scoring opportunities, Tiago Ribeiro and Vinicius Lopes found the back of the net in either half to fire Santa Clara to victory, leaving the hosts to rue their poor finishing.

Head coach Petit will be delighted with the result at the Estadio do Maritimo, particularly after a difficult two weeks, with the Azoreans suffering a 3-2 extra-time defeat against Mafra in the Taca de Portugal third round on October 18, eight days before losing 2-1 at home to Benfica to record their first Primeira Liga defeat of the season.

Having finished 13th in the league last season, their lowest league rank since their relegation in 2023, Santa Clara have taken giant strides this season, picking up six wins and three draws from their opening 10 games to sit fourth in the Primeira Liga table, level on 21 points with third-placed Sporting CP.

Key to Santa Clara’s promising start has been the solid job at the defensive end of the pitch, where they are one of the most disciplined sides in the divisions, conceding just six goals and keeping five clean sheets so far — only league leaders Porto have conceded fewer (4).

On the other hand, Gil Vicente failed to arrest their slump in form last weekend when they were held to a goalless draw by Vitoria de Guimaraes at the Estadio Cidade de Barcelos.

Having opened October with three consecutive victories, including a 3-2 extra-time victory over Uniao Santarem in the Taca de Portugal third round on October 14, Gil Vicente have since endured a downturn in form, going three straight games without a win (1D 2L), a run which saw them crash out of the Taca da Liga courtesy of a 4-1 hammering at the hands of Benfica on October 29.

Despite their recent struggles, Gil Vicente have plenty of positives to draw from, having picked up four wins and three draws from their 10 Primeira Liga games to collect 15 points and sit seventh in the league standings.

Having picked up back-to-back victories over Moreirense and Braga in their last two Primeira Liga away games, Luis Pinto’s men will be relying on their recent improvement on the road as they look to get back on their feet this weekend.

However, a daunting away challenge awaits Gil Vicente at the Estadio de Sao Miguel, where they are on a run of four consecutive defeats and have failed to win each of their last eight visits since a 2-0 victory in September 2015.

Santa Clara will have to cope without Portuguese midfielder Pedro Ferreira, who is set to sit out his second consecutive game after sustaining an injury against Benfica on October 26.

He is joined on the Azoreans’ injury table by 25-year-old defender Matheus Araujo, who continues his return to full fitness after suffering a severe knee injury last December.

Meanwhile, Gil Vicente remain without the services of 21-year-old midfielder Mohamed Bamba, who has been out of action since January due to a severe knee injury.

Jose Silva was forced off injured late in the game against Guimaraes last time out and the 21-year-old defender is out of contention for the trip to Estadio de Sao Miguel, while Frenchman Arthur Tchaptchet also continues his spell on the sidelines.

Neneca; Soares, Pacheco, Fernandes, Romao; Borges, Ribeiro, Tavares; Lopes, Fernando, Brenner

Lucao; Moreira, Buatu, Esgaio, Silva; Prioste, Lausen; Toure, Garcia, Murilo; Franca

Santa Clara have put together a strong early-season form, and having displayed impressive ability to keep opponents at arm’s length so far, they look better equipped to control this one.

With just three goals scored in the last three meetings between Santa Clara and Gil Vicente, we anticipate another cagey affair this weekend, with Petit’s men coming away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

#1745. Man United 3-2 Roma PLAYER RATINGS: Which star delivered their best performance in a red shirt? Whose physicality is something to marvel at? And who deserves 3/10 for their abysmal defending?

Published: 17:21 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EDT, 4 November 2026

Manchester United pulled out an enormous win for Michael Carrick as they fought back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

Winless in nine games heading into this European night under the lights and United were staring at 10 without a win, a record that was last struck in 1978, when they were two down at half-time after a dreadful start.

But United conjured up spirit that has been barely visible so far this season as a brace from Matheus Cunha - who finished the night getting sent off - followed a penalty from Bruno Fernandes to seal the most crucial of wins.

What it means for Carrick's future in the medium to longer term remains to be seen.

Those upstairs at United have privately taken a lot of the blame and want to end the churn of managers carrying the can for poor player performances. Only time will tell how big a turning point this night can be.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT was at Old Trafford on a frantic night to run the rule over the players...

Matheus Cunha rescued victory from the jaws of defeat for Manchester United against Roma

Made a big save low to his right on the stroke of half-time to prevent further embarrassment for United and, as it turned out, give them a fighting chance of getting the result they pulled out of the hat. His distribution seems to have really regressed this season with far too many aimless balls, though.

Made a huge recovery tackle to deny Rodrigo Mora a third and in a feckless first half it was he who bust a gut where others didn't. Yes, it's a low bar but Yoro has actually been one of, if not, the best United performers during this never-ending malaise.

A performance littered with mistakes that, in truth, looked to have been scrubbed from his game coming into this campaign. He's the leader of the back-line and he did everything but lead in a first half that saw positioning and decision-making leave a lot to be desired. His clearance that resulted in Roma's second goal was diabolical. Booked and was fortunate not to have been sent off.

Harry Maguire left a lot to be desired in a defensive performance littered with basic errors

Thrust into the side in place of Lisandro Martinez and his head will have been spinning when he gave away a penalty for a handball, which Donyell Malen converted. Booked for a lunging challenge that is becoming a worrying trend of tackling with studs up. May sound daft but he needs coaching by Jonny Evans or Jonathan Woodgate on a better way to slide tackle. Booked.

Abysmal defending for Roma's first goal as he committed to the attack like a winger and left Matias Soule the freedom of Manchester to score. Kept pushing forward – you have to assume by instruction – and kept being found wanting. Options are slim but he's not making any positive contribution to the team from left back. Needs a stop putting to it.

Got told to 'f**k off' by Bruno Fernandes in a fraught first half for a bobbly pass to tee him up on the edge of the box. Made a couple of smart bursts through lines but he's in the side to protect the defence and he didn't do it. Night cut short when he pulled his hamstring 60 seconds into the second half.

Will be disappointed with himself at how sloppily he gave away the ball in a turnover which exposed his defenders for the first goal. That error aside, he settled in and improved as it wore on. His ability to actually beat a man is in short supply in this United side and his physicality was something to marvel at at times.

Kobbie Mainoo actually looks to drive past players, a skill in short supply at United

Always has a buzz about him when he gets the ball and he was the only one to come back from Como with any crumb of credit. Here it was a more sobering affair where his influence was heavily restricted and it means his wait for a United goal goes on. Not managed one since December 2025.

A night of frustration for large spells but one that did eventually serve up a goal and assist for the United captain. He was unfairly booked when Soule got into a pushing match that was very one sided down in the corner. Missed a second-half penalty (which was re-taken due to encroachment) and made no mistake second time around. All that aside, it was a poor look when he's berating team-mates when his own performance level is way below what he's capable of, mind you.

Comfortably the best player in a United shirt on the night - even with the red card. For one, he gets stuck in. For two, it was Cunha who won the penalty – however fortunate a decision that was – that Fernandes eventually converted to make it 2-1. He deserved an assist when he set Mbeumo free for a run on goal moments later. Scored two crucial late goals that will airbrush just how bad a tackle he made to see red. Could make a case for his best performance in a United shirt. It's up there.

Had his head in his hands, much like a lot of the supporters, when he struck both posts after being played through one v one by Cunha. Had a couple of opportunities to scamper through on goal but just didn't have the pace.

Bryan Mbeumo will want his second half breakaway chance back after striking both posts

Muted in celebration at the end and given everything he's had to navigate this season that's perhaps understandable. But this was a shot in the arm, how big we need to wait and see. People have labelled him a dead man walking but he's not giving up yet.

Youri Tielemans (for Carlos Baleba, 51) - 5

Did OK, but didn't do a great deal to drive the play forward. Not exactly the perfect foil to Mainoo, who is stylistically similar.

Lifted the crowd and helped change the game. Should have won a penalty when he was hacked down and it was his assist to Cunha that sealed victory. Coudln't have made a stronger case to start on Sunday.

Lisandro Martinez (for Ayden Heaven, 75) - 6

The fact he was far away from the eventual headlines was probably a good thing for all concerned after what transpired at Stamford Bridge.

#1743. Rennes vs Lille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 06 Nov 2026 21:33

Rennes welcome Lille to Roazhon Park on Sunday afternoon in round 10 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

In their previous league outing, Les Rouge et Noir fell to a disappointing 5-2 defeat against Nice at the Allianz Riviera, while Les Dogues snatched a late 1-0 win over Lens on home soil.

After agonisingly falling short of ending their six-year UEFA Champions League absence last season, losing 3-1 to Marseille on the final weekend to finish just two points outside the automatic qualification places, Rennes will be fairly content with how they have begun their latest Ligue 1 campaign.

Franck Haise’s men started the season in emphatic fashion, claiming victory in three of their opening four league games to sit joint top of the Ligue 1 table in the middle of September, but having picked up just six points from their five games since, Sunday’s hosts have slipped to fifth and have just one win in their latest five matches in all competitions.

Despite boasting an unbeaten start to their endeavours on the continent, Les Rouge et Noir will be slightly disappointed with their position in the UEFA Europa League table too, with Haise’s side currently 17th in the standings after drawing three of their opening four fixtures.

Having failed to win any of their previous seven encounters with Lille at Roazhon Park, dating back to a 3-1 triumph on the final day of the 2018-19 season, Rennes will be desperate to rediscover their winning touch this Sunday by ending that barren run and returning to form.

Following a much improved 2025-26 Ligue 1 campaign in which they finished third and booked their place in the Champions League, having only managed Europa League qualification the year prior, Davide Ancelotti will be extremely happy with how his side have started the current season.

With just one league loss so far, falling to a narrow defeat against Nice at the Allianz Riviera in September, Les Dogues have accumulated 18 points from their nine matches and sit second in the Ligue 1 standings, behind only back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain.

Over that span, Lille’s greatest strength has undoubtedly been their defensive solidity, with Sunday’s visitors keeping an impressive five clean sheets and conceding just six goals, a tally bettered by no other side inside France’s top three divisions.

Although much like their opposition, Les Dogues will be feeling extremely underwhelmed with their performances in Europe, as Tuesday evening’s goalless draw with Danish side Bodo/Glimt marks the first point Ancelotti’s men have earned in the competition this season, leaving them only above Slovan Bratislava at the foot of the Champions League standings.

However, having won three of the previous four meetings with Rennes, including an important 2-1 victory when they travelled to Roazhon Park in March, Lille will be confident of putting their European woes behind them on Sunday afternoon by claiming another three points in Ligue 1 and pushing towards Les Parisiens at the summit of the table.

Having netted seven goals in as many Ligue 1 games to start the season, Rennes will be hoping that Esteban Lepaul can finally make a return this weekend from an ankle injury that has kept him out of the previous month.

After missing Les Rouge et Noir’s previous league outing against Nice with a thigh issue, Brice Samba was back between the sticks during the week and is likely to start behind a back five including Bryan Reynolds, Charlie Cresswell and Mahamadou Nagida on Sunday.

Scoring three goals in his latest four matches in all competitions, Senegalese striker Boulaye Dia has stepped up as the hosts’ main goal threat in Lepaul’s absence and will be looking to add to his campaign tally of four Ligue 1 strikes against Lille.

Portuguese defender Tiago Santos and 24-year-old Moroccan Hamza Igamane are Lille’s only two confirmed absentees as they continue their recovery from cruciate ligament injuries, however the latter is expected to return in the coming months.

It remains to be seen whether Japanese forward Ayase Ueda features on Sunday after missing the previous month with a foot injury, though Ancelotti is likely to opt for either Olivier Giroud or Hakon Haraldsson through the middle regardless.

Algerian midfielder Nabil Bentaleb also missed Tuesday’s trip to Bodo/Glimt due to illness, making him a doubt for the weekend.

However, on a more positive note for the visitors, French defender Tanguy Nianzou is back available for selection on Sunday after serving a red card suspension against Lens and is almost certain to slot alongside Alexsandro at the back.

With both sides enjoying promising starts to the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign, Sunday’s clash is bound to be one of the highlights of the weekend and could easily go either way.

However, despite their recent struggles in the Champions League, it is extremely difficult to ignore Lille’s current surge towards the Ligue 1 summit, and we are backing them to maintain the pressure on PSG by collecting all three points this weekend.

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 06 Nov 2026 21:34

Atalanta BC will be looking to end a six-match winless run across all competitions when they travel to Monza on Sunday for matchday 11 of the Serie A campaign.

Maurizio Sarri's side sit 13th in the Italian top-flight table after collecting just 11 points from their opening 10 matches, leaving them four points above the relegation zone, where the hosts occupy 18th place.

Atalanta's struggles have continued into November, with a 3-0 home defeat to Parma in their most recent league outing leaving them without a Serie A victory in four matches since beating Venezia 3-1 on October 12.

That run has contributed to La Dea's weakest start to a Serie A season since 2014-15, having managed just three victories from their opening 10 fixtures, during which they have scored 16 goals and conceded 20, highlighting the need for greater balance at both ends of the pitch.

Sarri's men head into this encounter on the back of a 1-1 draw against Kairat Almaty at the New Balance Arena, where Nikola Krstovic scored an 82nd-minute equaliser, leaving the Bergamo outfit 16th in the league-phase table and still without a win in six outings across all competitions.

Atalanta will also be looking to secure their first league victory away from home this weekend after collecting just one point from their opening four Serie A away fixtures, although that came in their most recent trip, a 2-2 draw against Fiorentina.

Sarri has endured a difficult start to his first season in charge, although the former Lazio boss can take some encouragement from his record against Juric, having won five of their 12 previous managerial meetings and lost just twice, and will be hoping to improve that tally on Sunday in what promises to be an interesting reunion.

History in this fixture offers little encouragement for Monza, who have lost each of their previous four league meetings with Atalanta on their own turf and suffered defeat in all seven of their last competitive encounters, including a 4-0 thrashing in May 2025 that confirmed their relegation in the 2024-25 season.

#1740. Michael Carrick might STILL be one game from the sack. A one-night stand of epic proportions was up there with Man United's best but produced more questions than answers, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:31 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EDT, 4 November 2026

What a crazy, chaotic and, frankly, confusing night this was at Old Trafford. The grand old place has seen a few of them down the years, and Manchester United's incredible comeback win over Roma was right up there with the best.

By the end of it, the fans were loving United and hating the Glazers in keeping with their doctrine. Michael Carrick was savouring arguably his greatest moment as head coach, and yet might still be one game from the sack. Two-goal hero Matheus Cunha was being manhandled off the pitch and towards the tunnel, furious at not being able to celebrate with his teammates.

For Carrick, this felt like the equivalent of Erik ten Hag's win over Manchester City in the 2024 FA Cup final and Ruben Amorim's incredible 4-3 victory over Lyon in the Europa League quarter-final last year. The feelgood factor and sense of elation around Old Trafford was palpable.

Neither of those wins were enough to keep Ten Hag and Amorim in a job for much longer, and that is the conundrum for United bosses this morning.

If the feeling in the boardroom – and it remains an if – is to relieve Carrick of his duties, can they be swayed by a one-night stand, albeit one of epic proportions.

If United can follow this up with victory on Sunday over Aston Villa and Unai Emery – one of the candidates being touted as Carrick's replacement – can they really sack their head coach at the start of the international break?

Michael Carrick gave his players the half-time fire power needed to pull off a famous fightback

More than just pulling off the much-needed win against Roma, it felt as if his stars were playing for their manager

On another night when United fans turned on the Glazers, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, director of football Jason Wilcox and even the players as boos greeted the half-time whistle and the 'play like you mean it' banner made a re-appearance for the first time in three years, it was a reminder that the most popular person at the club might be the man who is about to get the bullet.

The players certainly looked as though they are playing for Carrick, and afterwards Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans both gave him their backing.

Looking ahead to this game, Carrick had said: 'Whatever happens is going to happen after that in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first.'

Those words came true in spectacular fashion. For a while, it felt as though he wouldn't even survive until the Villa game as United's defence fell apart and Roma set a new record for a European opponent taking a two-goal lead at Old Trafford. It could have been worse.

Carrick got his players together at half-time and reminded them that it only takes one moment to light the touchpaper here. 'I don't like talking to the lads too much about the history of this place, but it's magical,' he said. 'There's something when we have these nights and we do it the hard way, and one moment can flip the whole feeling.'

Kobbie Mainoo put it more bluntly. 'We needed a bit of a kick,' said the United midfielder.

It worked. United roared back at Roma, showing a resolve and strength of character that has been missing for much of this season. Fernandes converted a retaken penalty, Cunha levelled and then smashed home the winner late on to give United their first victory in 10 games.

The Brazilian's sending-off for removing his shirt after scoring the third and then committing a silly foul on Leonardo Balerdi meant he wasn't allowed to go on the pitch at the end, much to his indignation. Carrick and his staff were there to reinforce the point.

Results clearly haven't been good enough this season, but one of the criticisms levelled at Carrick is that performances have been even worse. The combination of those two factors have left him fighting to save his job.

On the flip side, it felt like this win and the nature of it counted double. One that raised the roof at Old Trafford and lifted the soul.

Yet for so long on Tuesday night, the mood among the United faithful was one of mutiny. They revived the anti-Glazer campaign by bringing green and gold balloons into the Stretford End, and let them loose as the two teams walked out.

Rather like the protests against the absent owners who keep a safe distance thousands of miles away in America, they were never going to hit their target by reaching the pitch and floated harmlessly into the night air. A barrage of tennis balls had greater impact, but they too were soon cleared out of sight.

Chants against the Glazers, Ratcliffe and Wilcox rang out long before kick-off. 'You can stick your new stadium up your a***' chanted the fans. The game was seconds old when we heard the first rendition of 'sell United and f*** off home' followed by the tribute song to Carrick.

Even at a critical point in the game when VAR was studying Gianluca Mancini's challenge on Cunha to see if it warranted a penalty, the United fans broke into a chorus of 'we want Glazers out'. It was the same after Cunha fired the decisive goal as supporters turned on the Americans and voiced their support for Carrick once more. They were caught between wanting to vent their anger at the owners and back Carrick and the team.

Fervent and continuing protests against the ownership underscored Carrick's own popularity, despite being potentially days from getting the sack

Matheus Cunha might have been the late hero but he was unable to celebrate with his team-mates and manager after taking off his shirt

'The players one hundred per cent feed off the crowd, absolutely no doubt whatsoever,' said Carrick. 'I understand there's frustration and disappointment, I totally get that.

'Probably the time when it was easy for them not to be there, they were there. I felt that there was frustration, of course there was. I get it. But I know what they're like and we've got to give them something to go on.'

United managed to do that in the end, but it was a funny sort of night. One that produced more questions than answers. The biggest of them concerns Carrick. Is he doing enough to convince his employers that United can turn a corner? Victory in Europe doesn't alter the fact they are one place above the Premier League relegation zone.

There is one more game against Villa and then the choice is very simple: stick or twist?

#1739. Crystal Palace vs Liverpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 22:19, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 08:29

Liverpool will hope to bounce back and deliver a fatal blow to Pierre Sage's hopes of remaining in charge of Crystal Palace when the two clash in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds are sixth in the top flight with 15 points after nine matchweeks, and the come into the weekend on the back of a 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, whereas Palace are 18th with just seven points and could end the weekend in last place.

Palace may soon find themselves on the lookout for a new manager, with Sage coming under immense pressure considering his side have won just once in their last seven games, and their 2-0 defeat against Tottenham Hotspur on October 31 was a particularly frustrating afternoon for the head coach.

Their latest result was a 1-1 stalemate with Hoffenheim on Thursday in the Europa League, and while the fact the Londoners managed to score a stoppage-time equaliser despite having 10 men on the pitch should be seen positively, it was still another match without victory.

The defensive solidity that had defined Oliver Glasner's reign has disappeared, with the Eagles having conceded the most goals in the Premier League (21).

Palace are not cut adrift in the relegation zone given only two points separate them from 15th-placed Fulham, but losing a fourth consecutive top-flight fixture would be hugely demoralising.

Selhurst Park has been far from the fortress that it has been in the past considering they have won just three of their seven homes contests this season, and it will be a serious concern to supporters that the hosts have lost three of their four Premier League games at the stadium so far.

Andoni Iraola's reign at Liverpool has been largely positive, but the club have now lost consecutive games, with their 1-0 loss against Arsenal on November 1 effectively ending any early hopes that the team could challenge for the title.

The Reds twice took the lead against Fenerbahce, only to concede four minutes after each time they scored, before Vedat Muriqi netted the winner 11 minutes from time.

Liverpool did enjoy impressive triumphs against Bournemouth, Brentford and Brighton & Hove Albion in their five most recent league outings, and their only defeats in the top flight have come against Manchester City and Arsenal.

However, it cannot be ignored that the Merseysiders have scored just 11 goals in nine Premier League clashes this season, with striker Alexander Isak receiving little service in the penalty area.

While the Reds were beaten 2-1 by Palace when they last travelled to Selhurst Park in September 2025, they won 10 of their prior 11 meetings with the Eagles at the stadium.

It should also be noted that Liverpool's defeat against Fenerbahce was their first loss on the road this campaign, with Iraola having guided the team to four victories from their six away trips so far.

The most obvious problem for Palace to solve is how to replace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta, who received a red card for a dangerous tackle on Tottenham's Micky van de Ven.

Ismaila Sarr could have been an option to lead the line, but he is also injured, so perhaps Eddie Nketiah will start his fourth Premier League match of the season, supported by Evann Guessand and Yeremi Pino.

Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton are likely to patrol the middle of the pitch ahead of defenders Jaydee Canvot, Axel Disasi and Chris Richards.

Liverpool knew before the start of the season that they would be without the likes of Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni for much of 2026, but there are growing concerns about Ryan Gravenberch's heel fracture.

The midfielder was left out entirely on Wednesday, and while he could play through the pain barrier, it would be surprising if he was even in the squad.

Trey Nyoni is deserving of a spot alongside Alexis Mac Allister, but the 19-year-old has started his side's last two games, therefore Iraola will almost certainly opt to rest the youngster in favour of Dominik Szoboszlai.

Henderson; Canvot, Disasi, Richards; Khalaili, Wharton, Kamada, Mitchell; Pino, Guessand; Nketiah

Palace may boast the advantage of playing at home, but their lack of options in attack could cost them.

While Liverpool have been far from perfect in the final third, they have often taken three points from Selhurst Park, and it would not be surprising if they claimed another victory on the road this weekend.

A red card for the substitute Yusif threatened to change the momentum of the game, but the Rossoneri were unable to fashion any real response to put the result in doubt in what was another forgettable European night.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that beat Inter in the derby, with Lorenzo Torriani, Filippo Terracciano, Davide Bartesaghi, Ardon Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse coming into the team.

Ferencvaros started the game on top and they created the first big chance of the game less than four minutes in. A loose pass as Milan tried to build out was seized upon by Zachariassen who threaded Joseph through, and though his initial attempt was blocked by Koni De Winter, the forward managed to get another shot off from a few yards out that was thankfully straight at Torriani.

The first 15 minutes were quite frankly dreadful from Milan, in complete contrast to the victory at the weekend. The away side dominated possession thanks to so many sloppy giveaways, and Birmancevic nearly found himself bearing down on goal in a central area though he fired at his own man after some good close control.

It continued to be all the Hungarian side as the majority of the San Siro crowd began to grow worried and impatient. Another shot towards the goal came in the 17th minute, and even if Zachariassen did roll it straight at Torriani the fact he was found in space beyond the defensive line caused more worry.

Milan did not grow into the game as hoped and the errors kept coming. A stray pass backwards from Jashari under pressure put Joseph through on goal for Ferencvaros, though Torriani read his shot towards the bottom right corner well and was able to claim it. Another warning sign, however.

The first half was probably best summarised by two fouls in quick succession. The first saw Cisse act on the frustration of losing the ball and go lunging in to earn a yellow card that in fairness to the youngster was harsh, then Bartesaghi lost possession near the touchline before clumsily bundling his man over to give away a free-kick.

It took until the 39th minute for Milan to have their first shot of the game, but Cisse lashed it well over the bar from an Adrien Rabiot knock-down that landed nicely just beyond the penalty spot. At the other end, Joseph got the better of Diawara to surge into the box, yet Torriani was equal to his effort from a very narrow angle.

Torriani was by far the busier of the two goalkeepers and he was called into action again a few minutes from the break, with Joseph again the man who found space to shoot inside the box. The Italian got a strong hand to thwart the angled drive.

Amorim was clearly very displeased with what he saw in the first half, as he chose to make three changes at the break, bringing on Mario Gila, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic. Diawara, Cisse and Yunus Musah were the ones to come off.

Milan started the second half the better of the two sides, with Hutchinson firing into the side netting and then Ramos going on a winding run past three players into the box before a deflected shot.

Seven minutes into the second half, the deadlock was finally broken and it was unfortunately a moment to forget for Torriani. De Winter played a bit of a demanding pass back to the goalkeeper inside the box and the heavy first touch was seized upon, with the Ferencvaros player going down for what would have been a penalty had Joseph not been on hand to slot into an empty net.

The Rossoneri’s response was almost instant with Ramos again at the centre of some good work on the edge of the box, feeding Hutchinson’s run beyond the last man down the left side of the box, though the shot across goal just rolled wide of the far post.

In the 66th minute, Ferencvaros dealt Milan a sucker punch as they doubled their advantage just after Jashari had come off for Luka Modric. A bit of a ricochet in midfield led to a dangerous two-on-one situation for the visitors, allowing Zachariassen to lay it on a plate to Joseph, who simply had to slot it into an empty net.

The final change came just after with Francesco Camarda coming on for Bartesaghi, and he was not far from reopening the contest with a near-post flick from Moreira’s cross. Up the other end, a quickly taken free-kick saw Zachariassen’s half-volley draw a reaction save from Torriani.

There was a moment of madness from the substitute Yusuf with 15 minutes left on the clock as he seemed to reach out an elbow to strike Gila unprovoked. The Spaniard went down, VAR took a look and the referee sent him off.

Dibusz hadn’t been very busy all night, but the veteran goalkeeper was called upon to make a good save with his legs from Hutchinson’s shot through a crowd. It was looking more and more like not being the Diavolo’s night.

Ferencvaros should have had a third in the second of four added minutes when another loose pass towards Torriani was collected by Madarasz, who rounded the keeper but hit the side-netting.

#1737. Predicted Brentford XI vs. Brighton: Yehor Yarmoliuk returns as one attacking change made

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 22:39, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 02:41

Brentford midfielder Yehor Yarmoliuk is set to start Sunday’s Premier League away clash against Brighton & Hove Albion.

The midfielder is available for selection after serving a three-match ban for the red card he picked up in the 2-1 defeat to Liverpool on October 17.

Yarmoliuk was a regular starter before his suspension, so he is expected to replace Mamadou Sangare in the middle of the park for Sunday’s trip to the south coast.

The Ukraine international is likely to line up alongside Vitaly Janelt, while Mathias Jensen is set to operate in an advanced position as Brentford exercise caution with Mikkel Damsgaard, who has been dealing with a foot issue since the last international break.

Kevin Schade and Jaidon Anthony could provide the threat from out wide, the latter of whom is pushing to replace Dango Ouattara after coming off the bench to provide an assist in the 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Meanwhile, Brentford’s record signing Jannik Schuster will once again have to settle for a place on the bench, with Kristoffer Ajer and Sepp Van den Berg set to resume their central defensive partnership after keeping a clean sheet last time out.

They will offer the last line of protection to Caoimhin Keller, along with Michael Kayode and Keane Lewis-Potter, who will feature on the right and left sides of defence respectively.

In regard to absentees, Antoni Milambo remains unavailable for selection despite closing in on his long-awaited return from injury.

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews is also without the injured quartet of Kaye Furo, Fabio Carvalho, Josh Dasilva and Rico Henry.

#1736. Unai Emery has closed gap between Aston Villa and Europe's elite - but rampant Barcelona proved there is still a way to go as Lamine Yamal dazzles, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 17:17 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:27 EDT, 4 November 2026

John McGinn heard the question. His eyes darted around Barcelona's packed media auditorium for a second or two on Monday night. What was it like to be about to play in the Nou Camp, the Aston Villa skipper had been asked, as if this were to be some sort of spin off from Bill and Ted's Excellent Adventure.

McGinn was careful with his answer. He did not seek to downplay the nature of the occasion or the thrill that comes with lining up in such a majestic arena. But he was determined not to play the wide-eyed ingenu. 'What our club is trying to do now,' McGinn said, 'is make this normal, make this a yearly experience.'

So when he and his team-mates walked up the flight of steps from the dressing rooms into the vast bowl of the stadium on Tuesday evening, they were here to show that they were not arrivistes. Villa is a historic club. They won this competition in 1982, ten years before Barcelona ever did. They were not here for a treat or to get patted on the back just for turning up.

It is nearly 20 years since Liverpool became the last English club to win here and nobody gave Villa too much chance of ending that drought. They are being told constantly that the odds are stacked against them and that their much-admired manager, Unai Emery, may be tempted by the entreaties of struggling 'giants' elsewhere.

That was the reason why this game early in the league phase had attained so much importance. For Villa, it was a symbol of something they aspire to. They want to get used to belonging in this company, to walking up those steps, to emerging into the stadium in the pouring rain, and staring at players of the calibre of Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Pau Cubarsi staring back at them.

It still feels as if they stand on the cusp of something bigger but they blew their shot at proving that on Tuesday night. They needed to be at their best to have a chance of beating Hansi Flick's side, which sits atop LaLiga, and they were far too naïve in defence to get close to causing a shock. They are rising but this was a step too far at this stage of their evolution.

Lamine Yamal (centre) and Barcelona had plenty to smile about after beating Aston Villa 3-0

Yamal opened the scoring for Barcelona after just seven minutes with this left-footed finish

Raphinha (right) doubled Barca's lead after half-time with this strike at the Spotify Nou Camp

The Nou Camp, which is still in the midst of an extensive renovation and was only about two-thirds full, was ringed by towering yellow cranes, peering down at the floodlit patch of green. From their lofty vantage point, they saw Villa get off to the worst possible start.

Only seven minutes had gone when Emery's team gift-wrapped a present for the home side. Zion Suzuki played the ball out short to Joao Gomes but Gomes panicked under pressure from the Barcelona press and the close attention of Pedri. He played the ball square without looking, straight to Yamal.

Of all the players he could have found, Gomes had to find Yamal. The Spain superstar squared up Pau Torres and then curled the ball around him with a gentle caress of his left boot. Suzuki was helpless. The ball nestled in the corner of the net. Barcelona had scored 56 goals in 14 games before this match. Extending the hand of generosity to them must have felt particularly galling for Emery.

Villa almost hit back immediately. A stinging volley from Matty Cash was deflected wide and Barcelona looked jittery at the back. Nicolas Jackson played a square ball to Johan Manzambi, who should have equalised but scuffed his first-time effort wide of Joan Garcia. Barcelona were thankful for Garcia's intervention when he raced out of his goal to dispossess Jackson as he charged on to a through ball.

Yamal was rampant. His battle with Ian Maatsen was a mismatch and Maatsen was booked after 11 minutes for hacking him down. Villa were still intent on playing themselves into trouble. Suzuki repeated his mistake when he tried to play the ball out to Joao Gomes. This time, Pedri beat him to it and the loose ball fell to Gordon. Gordon hit his shot towards the corner but Suzuki redeemed himself by diving to push it away.

Barcelona had the better of the play. They looked like scoring every time they went forward. Time and again, either Raphinha or Yamal found space to run at the Villa defence, which was barely coping. Even in that context, though, it was an open game. Villa had chances, too. Manzambi forced a fine save out of Garcia. A Jackson breakaway was thwarted by a last-ditch block.

But seven minutes after the break, Barcelona doubled their lead. Fermin Lopez played a clever ball to Raphinha, who had found a yard of space in the box. Raphinha, LaLiga's leading scorer this season, drilled a left-foot shot goalwards and it deflected off the heel of Torres, wrong-footed Suzuki and rolled over the line.

Barcelona put the game out of reach midway through the half when Joao Cancelo forced his way past McGinn on the left flank and hit a sumptuous cross into the box with the outside of his right foot. Raphinha gambled on the path of the ball, darted behind his marker and tucked the ball away.

Raphinha completed the scoreline with this cute finish as Barcelona completed their victory

For Aston Villa, this will be a learning curve as they look to go far in the Champions League

Villa manager Unai Emery will have plenty to think about after another Nou Camp defeat

Substitute Leon Goretzka hit the face of a post for Villa late on but the game was already gone. There was no shame in losing to a team who are one of the favourites to win the competition this season but there was frustration in the way Villa had handed their opponents the advantage.

Emery looked bedraggled as he stood on the touchline in the rain, arms folded, shaking his head. This was his 15th defeat in 16 visits to the Nou Camp. As Villa's coach fights to edge his team closer to the elite of the game, this game will become just one more bad memory.

#1735. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.
