#1660. Opinion: Liverpool make Ronald Araujo decision, major update proves it

Ronald Araujo has been one of Liverpool's best signings this season.

The defender came to Anfield on a season-long loan in their time of need.

Most people thought that he would just be a back-up option that could cover centre-back and right-back if needed.

However, his stellar performances since the start of the campaign have led to him making the right-back spot his own with others such as Jeremie Frimpong and Joe Gomez failing to displace him.

As mentioned, he's only on a season-long loan at the moment with Liverpool's option to buy worth somewhere around €55 million.

This price tag has created a bit of a stumbling block for the Reds with a decision on his future now potentially being made.

Liverpool may sign Nmamdi Collins instead of Ronald Araujo

Liverpool's defence has been a major topic of conversation over the last couple of years.

Whether it's been players such as Trent Alexander-Arnold leaving or fans questioning why they spent £55 million on Jeremy Jacquet, the Reds' defence has always been a huge topic.

And, with Virgil van Dijk, Alisson and Gomez's contracts all expiring in June 2027, it's going to remain at the centre of attention for some time.

Figuring out what's going to happen with their current crop of players is likely to be one of the main things holding up a deal for Araujo.

But, as per a fresh update from Fussball News, a totally different target than the Uruguayan seems to have just made his way onto Liverpool's shortlist.

"According to information from fussball-news.de, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool are all seriously interested in the Frankfurt defender. All three Premier League clubs are monitoring his development and regularly scout the young German international," they wrote.

"A departure from Frankfurt in the near future doesn't seem likely. The club from Hesse is planning for the long term with Collins and only recently secured his services with a contract extension until the summer of 2030.

"Nevertheless, the defender could become an interesting prospect in the upcoming transfer windows. "Collins' versatility is a major draw for top English clubs. The right-footed player can be deployed both in central defense and on the right side of defense.

"In addition, he possesses exceptional speed, physical presence, and tackling skills. Collins can particularly exploit his athletic strengths against fast attacking players."

Nmamdi Collins would be a better option for Liverpool than Ronald Araujo

Right now, fans would hate to see Araujo not get given a permanent deal.

However, since he'll be 28 years old by next summer, he may not have all that long left at the top.

Obviously, if his performances keep to this same level throughout the entire campaign, Liverpool will have to heavily consider signing him permanently.

But, it certainly won't hurt for them to weigh up their options.

Collins is much less experienced than Araujo and hasn't tried his luck outside of the Bundesliga yet but, since he's so important for Eintracht Frankfurt despite only being 22 years old, he's clearly an exceptional talent.

The report from Fussball News also goes on to say that a fee worth around €35 million is all that would be required for Liverpool to sign him.

This price tag is a much lower risk to Liverpool and since he's still so young, he could very easily grow to become an even better player than he already is.

At the moment, nobody knows what the Reds are going to do but, if their back line isn't a major area of focus again in the upcoming transfer windows, it'll be a massive shock.

#1659. Man United transfer news: Barcelona's Alejandro Balde January stance 'revealed' amid Old Trafford links

By Ben Sully | 07 Nov 2026 01:55, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 02:32

Manchester United have reportedly been handed encouragement in their potential pursuit of Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde.

The 23-year-old enjoyed plenty of playing time last term, starting 31 of his 42 competitive matches across all competitions.

However, he was linked with a move away in the summer window after learning that he would have to settle for a squad role this season.

Man United were among those linked with the left-back, but he ultimately remained at the Camp Nou after being reluctant to give up on his Barcelona career.

Balde has gone on to make just five competitive appearances this term and is still waiting for his first start of the season, with Hansi Flick preferring to use Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart.

While Espart is currently sidelined with an ankle problem, there is little sign that Balde's playing situation will dramatically improve unless further injuries force Flick's hand.

After being pushed to the fringes of the Barcelona squad, Balde has supposedly 'accepted' that he needs to leave Camp Nou to reignite his stalling career.

According to The Athletic, the Catalan giants are also open to the prospect of sanctioning Balde's departure in 2027.

Barcelona are even believed to be willing to entertain offers in the January window as they look to make a big sale to boost their chances of making a significant signing in the winter market.

However, Barcelona's negotiating position is somewhat weakened by the fact Balde has less than two years remaining on his current contract.

Barcelona's transfer stance should offer encouragement to Man United, who are searching for a new left-back after failing to strengthen the position in the summer.

Luke Shaw remains the club's first-choice left-back, but his injury issues have required the versatile Diogo Dalot to fill in during his absence.

However, the Red Devils will be keen to recruit a high-quality full-back who has the quality and potential to become the club's new first-choice option.

While Balde may be a viable target, the uncertainty surrounding Michael Carrick's future is a hindrance when it comes to drawing up January plans.

Ideally, Man United will want to sign a full-back who fits the head coach's style of play, which would likely be different if an Antonio Conte or Eddie Howe were to take over the reins.

#1658. Report: Andoni Iraola wants versatile defender at Liverpool now

Liverpool have a lot of changes that they need to make to their squad over the next few months.

By June 2027, a decent chunk of their first-team will be out of contract and, while some deals may end up being renegotiated, thus extending their stays, there are no talks going off between Liverpool and any of their players at the moment.

Obviously, this could change by the time the January transfer window comes around as, by then, any players with six months left on their contracts will be able to talk to foreign clubs about a free transfer.

So, before that happens, some deals may need to be ironed out so that the Reds can get ahead of their rivals in the transfer market.

And, fortunately for Liverpool's fanbase, Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward both seem to have found a player that they'd like to bring in.

Liverpool have been contacted about the transfer of Alejandro Balde

Nmamdi Collins is going to be one of the most talked about players in football ahead of the January transfer window.

The defender is only 22 years old but, he's become one of Eintracht Frankfurt's most important players.

Collins has featured in 69 games for the Bundesliga outfit over the last few years and, whether he's been used as a centre-back or a right-back, he's always found a way to stand out from the crowd.

Obviously, due to his importance to Frankfurt, they're rather reluctant to sell but, as per a fresh update from Fussball News, that hasn't stopped Liverpool from showing an interest in him.

"According to information from fussball-news.de, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool are all seriously interested in the Frankfurt defender. All three Premier League clubs are monitoring his development and regularly scout the young German international," they wrote.

"A departure from Frankfurt in the near future doesn't seem likely. The club from Hesse is planning for the long term with Collins and only recently secured his services with a contract extension until the summer of 2030.

"Nevertheless, the defender could become an interesting prospect in the upcoming transfer windows.

"Collins' versatility is a major draw for top English clubs. The right-footed player can be deployed both in central defense and on the right side of defense.

"In addition, he possesses exceptional speed, physical presence, and tackling skills. Collins can particularly exploit his athletic strengths against fast attacking players."

Nmamdi Collins could be exactly who Liverpool need to sign

Collins is probably a player that most fans won't have heard of.

But, the fact that he can play as a centre-back or a right-back perfectly well despite only being 22 years old is a massive achievement.

During his time with Frankfurt, the youngster has contributed to five goals across all competitions and, while this may not seem all that impressive, when he's played 30 of his 69 games with the Bundesliga outfit as a centre-back, it shows how prolific he can be.

Obviously, thanks to his importance to Frankfurt, a deal wouldn't come cheap but, since he's never really been tested outside of Germany, there's also an element of risk within the deal that needs to be taken into consideration.

At the moment, these are just rumours but, with how many players Liverpool still need to sign, bringing some lesser-known players such as Collins through the Anfield doors could be the best way for them to bolster their ranks.

#1656. Freiburg vs Union Berlin - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 02:50, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 04:17

A rebalanced Freiburg will welcome relegation-threatened Union Berlin to Europa-Park Stadion on Sunday, hoping to keep their unlikely Bundesliga title challenge alive.

Die Breisgau-Brasilianer are searching for a fourth win on the bounce, while Die Eisernen are eyeing a first victory in five games.

Julian Schuster's Freiburg set a blistering pace across the initial stages of this season, stealing a march on the likes of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund to lead the Bundesliga after five matches.

However, Die Breisgau-Brasilianer hit a stumbling block when they were beaten 2-1 by Bayer Leverkusen on October 18, and followed up that defeat with two more - 3-0 at Monaco in the Conference League and 3-1 to Bayern in the German top flight.

That being said, Schuster's side have found their feet once again ahead of this weekend, with Thursday's 1-0 continental triumph over Trabzonspor marking a third consecutive win across all competitions.

Last time out in the Bundesliga, Freiburg came from behind to secure all three points in a 2-1 victory at Augsburg, courtesy of Igor Matanovic's fourth league goal of the season and an 85th-minute winner from 21-year-old Cyriaque Irie.

That success has Die Breisgau-Brasilianer third in the table, where their tally of 16 points puts them just two shy of leaders Bayern and second-placed Dortmund.

With that in mind, a fourth straight win could see Schuster's men go top on Sunday, though the manager will also be wary of the fact his team sit only three points above seventh-placed Elversberg.

Meanwhile, Mauro Lustrinelli's Union lost three of their first four Bundesliga outings this season, immediately putting them in the relegation zone, but they appear to have turned a corner.

Die Eisernen collected a point in a 1-1 draw with FC Koln last weekend, when they were unable to hold out after Janik Haberer gave them the lead with just 10 minutes on the clock.

That stalemate may have been frustrating at the time, but Lustrinelli will be pleased with the broader context, which shows that his team are unbeaten across their past four league games, winning once.

Such newfound resilience has seen Union earn six of their seven-point total during that four-match run, and they now sit 16th in the table, two points behind all of the clubs up to 11th-placed Augsburg.

The Berliners' next target will be to escape the relegation zone entirely, but they will arrive at Europa-Park Stadion as underdogs and aware of the fact Schalke 04 are just one point behind in 17th.

Freiburg have a generally fit squad for this clash, though midfielder Patrick Osterhage is a doubt due to a muscle problem that saw him sit out against Trabzonspor.

Thankfully for Schuster, Maximilian Eggestein and Yannik Engelhardt should be ready to start in his double pivot behind the more attack-minded Yuito Suzuki.

As for Union, they are missing Stanley Nsoki due to a calf injury, while fellow centre-back Felix Uduokhai is serving the final game of his suspension after being sent off during the 1-1 draw with Augsburg on October 24.

Wing-back options Andrik Markgraf and Robert Skov are also unavailable once again, so Marvin Friedrich, Rani Khedira and Zeno Van Den Bosch may form the visiting back three, flanked by Janik Haberer and Derrick Kohn.

Likewise, Aljoscha Kemlein is set to be sidelined on Sunday, though Andras Schafer and Michel Aebischer will be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, striker Andrej Ilic is a doubt as he builds fitness following a lengthy layoff, but Tim Skarke and Livan Burcu should operate in a partnership up top, supported by Kastriot Imeri.

Backhaus; Treu, Ginter, Lienhart, Makengo; Eggestein, Engelhardt; Beste, Suzuki, Scherhant; Matanovic

Freiburg have rediscovered their form after a brief blip, and will be confident of taking all three points against one of the bottom three on Sunday.

However, Union have proven resilient in recent weeks and are unlikely to be easily beaten, so expect a close contest.

#1654. Hoffenheim vs Schalke 04 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 03:51, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 04:22

Relegation-threatened Schalke 04 will travel to SNP Arena on Sunday, hoping to catch floundering Bundesliga opponents Hoffenheim off guard before the international break.

Die Kraichgauer are looking for a first win in four games, while Die Knappen are desperate to avoid a fifth defeat in six matches.

Christian Ilzer's Hoffenheim were surprise contenders for Champions League football last season, and though they fell agonisingly short by finishing fifth, the club were aiming to build on that success.

However, Die Kraichgauer have endured a campaign of fluctuations, kicking off this term by losing four of their first five Bundesliga clashes before recording a trio of successive victories in the middle of last month.

Unfortunately for Ilzer, the pendulum of his team's form has swung back towards the negative once again, as the hosts prepare for this contest having failed to come out on top in any of their last three matches across all competitions, losing twice.

On Thursday, Hoffenheim suffered their latest frustration when they conceded a 91st-minute equaliser in a 1-1 Europa League draw with Crystal Palace, who had been reduced to 10 men when Adam Wharton was shown a second yellow card.

In the two games prior, Die Kraichgauer were eliminated from the DFB-Pokal in a penalty shootout against second-tier Holstein Kiel, before a 2-0 defeat at Werder Bremen last weekend.

That Halloween loss at the Weserstadion has left Ilzer's men 13th in the table with nine points, a tally that hardly provides security considering the club are sitting just two points above 16th-placed Union Berlin and three above their opponents in the automatic relegation spots.

Meanwhile, Miron Muslic's Schalke lifted the 2.Bundesliga title last term en route to their top-flight return, but they have fared the worst of any of the three promoted teams.

Die Knappen are 17th with only six points to their name after eight matches, and unless they avoid defeat, the club could find themselves at the bottom of the table for the international break, given they are just two points ahead of a rejuvenated Borussia Monchengladbach.

That fear could become reality on Sunday, with Muslic's side arriving in Sinsheim having lost four of their past five games across all competitions, including a 2-0 defeat to RB Leipzig last Saturday.

To make matters worse, the visitors are the lowest scorers in the entirety of the Bundesliga with four goals, and have blanked in each of their four most recent outings.

Schalke head to SNP Arena as significant underdogs and with little in the way of a silver lining to inspire hope, but Hoffenheim have been far from perfect this season, and Die Knappen know that a surprise win would likely lift them out of the bottom two, with Union set to face Freiburg.

Hoffenheim manager Ilzer made it clear in his press conference that the team have a number of players whose readiness will be examined closer to kick off, including right-back Vladimir Coufal (thigh) and versatile attacker Adam Hlozek (muscle).

The hosts are missing a slew of defenders, though, with Albian Hajdari (plantar fascia), Robin Hranac (meniscus) and Valentin Gendrey (fractured fibula) all unavailable, so Koki Machida and Ozan Kabak could start at the heart of Ilzer's backline, flanked by Bernardo and 18-year-old Natnael Abraha.

Midfielders Bambase Conte and Nathan De Cat are also sidelined due to respective adductor and meniscus injuries, though Wouter Burger and Leon Avdullahu should be on hand to start in the centre of the park, platforming Fisnik Asllani in the number 10 role.

Further forward, winger Patrick Wimmer is dealing with a muscle injury, but Alexander Prass and Adam Daghim will be ready to support striker Tim Lemperle up top.

As for Schalke, they are also missing defenders, with right-back Adrian Gantenbein (muscle) and centre-back Maximilian Wober (thigh) out, and the duo of Nikola Katic and Hasan Kurucay are expected to be joined by Timo and Vitalie Becker in their absence.

Janik Bachmann and fellow midfielder Ron Schallenberg are also dealing with hip and leg injuries, leaving Satoshi Tanaka and Soufiane El-Faouzi to start behind Kenan Karaman.

Elsewhere, striker Moussa Sylla could return from his left leg problem after the international break, but veteran Edin Dzeko looks set to lead the line on Sunday.

Baumann; Abraha, Machida, Kabak, Bernardo; Burger, Avdullahu; Prass, Asllani, Daghim; Lemperle

Karius; T Becker, Katic, Kurucay, V Becker; Tanaka, El-Faouzi; Ljubicic, Karaman, Aouchiche; Dzeko

Hoffenheim have struggled once again in recent weeks, but they will be quietly confident about their chances of beating one of the division's relegation favourites on Sunday.

Schalke's troubles in front of goal are well-documented, and it would be a surprise to see them find the back of the net, never mind walk away with anything from this clash.

#1653. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1652. Amorim offers honest Milan reflection: “We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team”

Ruben Amorim continued the criticism of his AC Milan side after their dismal defeat to Ferencvaros, branding them ‘not ready’ to compete on multiple fronts.

Amorim made the decision to enact six changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Inter convincingly in the derby at the weekend, but it backfired as his team never got going last night and were well-beaten by the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is reported that after the game the Portuguese coach gave a long speech to his players about their attitude and effort levels. Milan remain incredibly inconsistent on this front, as they continue to alternate very encouraging performances with disastrous and listless ones.

Amorim laid into his team during an interview with Sky after the final whistle, and then he spoke to the CBS Sports Golazo studio shortly afterwards. The exchange was transcribed by MilanNews.

Yesterday you were talking about identity, about character. Was this the difference?

“Yes, technically, tactically, and above all mentally, they were superior and deserved to win. Today we weren’t ready to play professional football, and I felt it. We need to look within ourselves and do better.”

And in the Champions League the level would be even higher…

“We have to focus on the small details, without thinking about the Champions League or anything like that. We just have to focus on improving the more specific aspects of football: the mentality, the heart, the passion. We have to improve on that.”

What is Ferencvaros’ level in European football, how do you rate them?

“I don’t know, it depends on the opponent, but they’re doing very well. They have four wins in four games, a clear identity, and today they were superior to us.”

What did this match tell you about Milan?

“That we’re not ready. We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team. We have moments, in some games, where we’re really strong, but then we can’t maintain our level, especially mentally. So this game told me and all of us that we’re not ready to be a very strong team.”

During the first half, I noticed you were very energetic on the sidelines, and then it almost seemed like you stopped giving directions. Can you tell there’s a certain lack of understanding within the team and that they’re not playing the way you’d like?

“No, I just do what I feel at the time, and sometimes I don’t do certain things just for show. We didn’t play well, that’s for sure; we had a completely different attitude in the last league game, while today we weren’t mentally prepared to fight for the win, and that’s what we need to work on.”

If there hadn’t been the derby at the weekend, do you think this match would have gone better?

“I have no idea, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter, we have to be ready to play every three days in different competitions. So it doesn’t matter if we had a match before or not. I think we have to improve a lot in all aspects of the game.”

Torriani played his first match as a starter. How do you rate his performance today?

“I think he did well in the first half. He had a difficult time with a pass, but Lorenzo doesn’t bear any responsibility for the team’s performance. In fact, in the first half he gave us time to try to make some changes in the second half. So Lorenzo just has to keep working. We have to improve as a team to be stronger.”

#1651. Report: Barcelona star loves what he's seeing at Liverpool, wants to follow suit

One Barcelona star likes what's happening at Liverpool right now. It's enough to make him want to follow suit.

Liverpool signed Ronald Araujo in the summer, bringing him in on loan from Barcelona. There’s an option to buy in there, for around £50m.

Will that option be triggered? It’s difficult to say. Back in the summer, it looked highly unlikely that Liverpool would ever trigger and expensive clause for a player essentially signed on a whim.

But Araujo’s efforts have been fantastic and he absolutely brings something to this squad that no one else does. He’s a rugged defender, one who thrives on physicality and wants to battle against other players. The Reds don’t really have other players like that, outside of Virgil van Dijk anyway.

So we think there’s actually a good chance that Araujo signs permanently. And that’s a fantastic turnaround for a player who Barcelona wanted rid of in the summer - this loan deal has completely rejuvenated his reputation.

Alejandro Balde follows suitBarcelona’s Alejandro Balde reportedly likes the look of what Araujo has done at Liverpool. That’s according to Sport, who claim the left-back is now open to moving on from Catalonia. Balde had the chance to do that in the summer, with plenty of clubs interested in his services. He rejected them, however, as he felt he could break back in with Barca. That’s not proven to be the case, though.

Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde reportedly likes the look of what Araujo has done at Liverpool. That’s according to Sport, who claim the left-back is now open to moving on from Catalonia.

Balde had the chance to do that in the summer, with plenty of clubs interested in his services. He rejected them, however, as he felt he could break back in with Barca. That’s not proven to be the case, though.

And so Balde apparently takes inspiration from Araujo in how positive a move away could be. He’s opened the door to other clubs and now his agent, Jorge Mendes, is in discussions about a transfer.

Funnily enough, one of those clubs is Liverpool. Balde could actually do exactly what Araujo has done, moving to Merseyside and rejuvenating his reputation there. There’s a very real chance it happens.

Liverpool do need a left-back, either in January or next summer, as Kostas Tsimikas’s contract is due to expire. They’re also just far from certain on what their best option there actually is and competition for Milos Kerkez is only a positive thing.

#1650. Arsenal vs. Hull: Why William Saliba must not start Premier League clash

By Ben Knapton | 07 Nov 2026 09:04

Ahead of Saturday's Arsenal vs. Hull City Premier League showdown, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton discusses why Mikel Arteta should hold back on starting William Saliba, and why the Gunner must embrace their 'boring' style of play.

Are Arsenal title favourites? Yes. That has been the case since the start of the season, even before it.

I will not say it is Arsenal's title to lose until it is literally one second from the final whistle with the title won. But the table suggests it probably is Arsenal's title to lose.

We are not even at the quarter-way point of the season, but Arsenal are top, deservedly so, and they have been the best team in the league. They can go six points clear with a win against Hull, with Man City not playing until the 5:30 game against Nottingham Forest.

What we have seen in recent weeks is that if Arsenal win the league again, it is going to be their defence that wins it for them. Ezri Konsa has been an absolute revelation, one of the signings of the season at the back.

When he came in, it would have been way too harsh to label him simply as Saliba cover. He was already at a very elite level with Aston Villa, but he has come in and slotted in seamlessly alongside Gabriel.

Now that Saliba is back and was on the bench against Slavia Prague, it has given Arteta an incredible defensive dilemma. Some Arsenal fans will want to see Saliba come straight back in, but he has not played at all since the World Cup and got no minutes in Prague, so he should be on the bench.

Either way, the defence is going to win us the title because there have been very few attacking masterclasses from Arsenal this season. They have only scored more than two goals in one Premier League game, and that was in the opening game against Coventry.

They should have scored more against Slavia Prague. There were moments in that game I thought they would be four or five-nil up.

Gyokeres put in a brilliant display with a lovely assist for Madueke and a good curling finish in off the post. But so many times in that game it felt like Arsenal just made the wrong decision, held on to the ball for far too long, got robbed of possession far too easily, and then conceded quite a poor goal near the end.

David Raya did not cover himself in glory for that goal, but neither did any player in a blue shirt in the Slavia Prague box.

Nevertheless, 10 points from 12 in the Champions League, three points clear at the top of the Premier League table. But when your team are the Premier League champions, you are always going to be demanding more.

There has been a lot of criticism of Arsenal's play this season, but I would rather keep winning 1-0 and win the title than win 4-0 or 5-0 a few times and not finish first.

If Arsenal's play style is difficult to watch, I will absolutely accept that if it wins us another Premier League title.

#1649. Spanish footballer, 30, dies after suffering cardiac arrest in sickening collision with goalkeeper which saw match abandoned

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and ELIANA SILVER, SENIOR FOREIGN NEWS REPORTER

Published: 02:34 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 19:08 EDT, 4 November 2026

A Spanish footballer has tragically died after suffering a severe blow to the chest in a collision with a rival goalkeeper during a match on Monday.

Jesus De ​Miguel, 30, of CD Tenerife, had been admitted to intensive care following a horrifying foul by FC Andorra goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono, which led to the Spanish second division match being abandoned deep into stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2.

His football club announced that De Miguel's condition had worsened overnight, with the forward passing away this morning.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

Tenerife, from Spain's second tier of football, confirmed De ​Miguel's death in a statement

Tenerife striker Jesus De ​Miguel has died following a collision during a Spanish second division match on Monday

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De ​Miguel, 30, had been admitted to intensive care following a horrifying collision with Andorra goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono (pictured)

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred (Picture from CD Castellon on Facebook)

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement this morning, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.'

'There are no words of comfort; There is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Journalist Ivan Alvarez reported that Owono, who is also Equatorial Guinea's national goalkeeper, 'is very affected by the situation and that the goalkeeper's intention is to apologise privately before making any public statements'.

UEFA has confirmed that a minute of silence will be held at all their matches this week in tribute to De Miguel.

'We are heartbroken by the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda,' president Aleksander Čeferin said.

'We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss.'

The Royal Spanish Footbal Federation have meanwhile cancelled all domestic matches today.

Tenerife's opponents FC Andorra offered their condolences following news of De Miguel's death, writing: 'With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.'

Football clubs across Spain, including Barcelona and Real Madrid, have led tributes following the news of the death.

'Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times,' Barcelona said in a statement.

Real Madrid also expressed their condolences, stating: 'Real Madrid wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club, and all his loved ones.'

The Spanish Footballers Association also released a statement, expressing their 'deepest sorrow' at the footballer's death.

'His loss leaves a huge void among those of us who shared his passion for football, his commitment to the footballers' community, and his work defending the rights of our fellow professionals,' the statement continued.

'The Board of Directors, all the staff of AFE, and the footballers' community wish to extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to his teammates at Club Deportivo Tenerife. In these moments of immense sadness, we send them all our love, support, and solidarity. You will always be part of our family.'

CD Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel was stretchered off the field after a collision with FC Andorra's Jesus Owono

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

De Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 30 appearances to help secure the team promoted from the Spanish third division as champions.

The forward had previously helped to secure Internacional de Madrid and CD Castellón promotions from the fourth and third divisions, respectively.

CD Castellon also released a statement on Tuesday morning in tribute to their former player, saying: 'With broken hearts and inconsolable grief, Club Deportivo Castellón bids farewell to Jesús De Miguel.

'Words fail to express the profound injustice of this loss. He wore this shirt with pride, celebrated goals with our fans at the SkyFi Castalia stadium, and was an integral part of a story that this fanbase will never forget.

'We extend our deepest condolences to his family and loved ones, offering them our heartfelt support during this difficult time. We also join CD Tenerife and its fans in mourning, sharing this sorrow with them. You will always be one of us, Demi. Rest in peace.'

Last September, another Spanish player died aged only 19 after a collision sent him into cardiac arrest.

Raul Ramirez Osorio, who played for fifth-tier team Colindres, jumped to grab the ball when he crashed into a rival player.

He immediately fell to the ground unconscious where his manager and a nursing student attempted to revive him, before he was taken to hospital.

He suffered a second cardiac arrest on his way there and after two days in the ICU tragically passed away.

And a few months ago was the 95th anniversary of a similar tragedy, involving Celtic goalkeeper John Thomson who died aged 22 after receiving a serious head injury.

During the match in September of 1931, Thomson dived at the feet of his Rangers rival Sam English to stop a ball, before hitting his head on his opponent's knee.

He was left unconscious with a bleeding head, before being taken to hospital, where he sadly died.

#1648. Julian Ward, pay whatever it takes to sign Liverpool the next Leo Messi, £160m is a steal

Julian Ward, we're begging you. Sign Liverpool the next Lionel Messi, no matter what it takes.

Liverpool have had a philosophy over the last few transfer windows. They should sign the best players available to them, regardless of their actual position, and then make things work with what they've got.

The idea is to maximise talent in the squad, instead of maximising 'fit', as was the strategy under Jürgen Klopp. Klopp would prefer not to sign someone unless there was a clear place in the team for them.

That hasn't been the case over the last couple of summers. Liverpool signed two near-identical strikers in 2025 with Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké not being obvious striker partners.

Then things moved up a gear in 2026 as the Reds built a squad with four left-wingers, no right-wingers, and a selection of midfielders who all largely do the same thing. Some would argue this is suboptimal.

But if that's the strategy then that's the strategy and we say go all in.

The next Lionel MessiWill there be a next Lionel Messi? Probably not in terms of skill and impact. But then they said that about Diego Maradona until Messi came along. Regardless, the Inter Miami star has now stepped away from the Argentina national team and that means a successor has to take up his number 10 shirt. Argentina are delaying that decision for this international break - no one will wear it while they decide who deserves it. The most likely successor? Nico Paz. Paz is the next-big-thing from Argentina, even if he's not actually from there. He was born in Tenerife, though his dad, former Argentina international Pablo Paz, clearly held some sway here. That decision to play for Argentina means they've now got the most exciting young talent in football on their books. Maybe Lamine Yamal still has something to say about that, but Paz has been absolutely ridiculous this season and looks set to explode to another level.

Will there be a next Lionel Messi? Probably not in terms of skill and impact. But then they said that about Diego Maradona until Messi came along.

Regardless, the Inter Miami star has now stepped away from the Argentina national team and that means a successor has to take up his number 10 shirt. Argentina are delaying that decision for this international break - no one will wear it while they decide who deserves it.

The most likely successor? Nico Paz. Paz is the next-big-thing from Argentina, even if he's not actually from there. He was born in Tenerife, though his dad, former Argentina international Pablo Paz, clearly held some sway here.

That decision to play for Argentina means they've now got the most exciting young talent in football on their books. Maybe Lamine Yamal still has something to say about that, but Paz has been absolutely ridiculous this season and looks set to explode to another level.

Now, we somewhat saw that coming as our Value Adder model has long held Paz as one of the most outstanding players in football. He's a threat with and without the ball, in and out of possession, and through goals and assists.

There aren't many like him and we view him as the next great star for Liverpool. Unfortunately, his form this season means everyone is catching up to that.

There is a problem with signing him, however. Fabrizio Romano has yet again pointed out that Real Madrid hold a buyback clause for Paz, sitting at around €80m next summer. They will almost certainly activate this.

The trick to signing Paz, then, is to convince Real Madrid to cash-in. Maybe that means paying twice that clause to sign him or some other ridiculous number, because Los Blancos don't technically need him.

They've got a wealth of attacking midfielders and goalscorers. We certainly can't see them playing through Paz as Como have, not when the likes of Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham are already there.

So there is a chance here to land a sensational player. You've just got to convince Real Madrid and that will only happen with an enormous offer. But we implore Julian Ward to make it. Paz is generational and almost certainly Messi's successor with Argentina.

#1647. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

#1645. Liverpool transfer news: Reds put on alert as Bayern Munich identify attacker as potential Diaz 'backup' option

By Ben Sully | 07 Nov 2026 09:38

Bayern Munich have reportedly placed Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha on their shortlist ahead of the January transfer window.

Ngumoha enjoyed a breakout season for the Reds last term, chipping in with three goal contributions in 29 competitive appearances.

The 18-year-old has started to take on a bigger role this season, demonstrated by the fact that he has started each of the club's four Champions League games.

Ngumoha has also made nine appearances across the Premier League and EFL Cup, with his encouraging displays earning him a call-up to Thomas Tuchel's latest England squad.

However, Tuchel is not the only one who has noticed Ngumoha's promising performances, as German giants Bayern are believed to be showing interest ahead of the January market.

According to Bild, Bayern have placed Ngumoha on a shortlist of potential 'backup' options for former Liverpool star Luis Diaz.

This is not the first time that Bayern have been linked with Ngumoha as they were believed to be interested in a summer deal before they recruited Ismael Saibari from PSV Eindhoven.

Vincent Kompany's side would ideally like to sign a young player who has the potential to grow into an important player.

While they are admirers of Ngumoha, Bayern have put the name of Porto's Oskar Pietuszewski at the top of their transfer shortlist.

They are also keen on Borussia Monchengladbach's Wael Mohya and Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi, the latter of whom is said to be a target for Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain.

Even if Bayern opted to pursue a move for Ngumoha, they would find it incredibly difficult to convince Liverpool to sanction a sale.

The teenager is seen as one of the Premier League's brightest attackers and possesses the potential to become a star for club and country in the years to come.

Ngumoha also has the trust of Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, who is willing to hand young stars their chance to impress, having also given the likes of Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni meaningful playing time this season.

With Ngumoha out of contract in 2028, the Reds are understood to be in discussions over a new long-term deal to ward off any potential transfer interest.

#1640. Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford opens up on "horrendous" Man City playing situation

By Ben Sully | 07 Nov 2026 10:03, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 10:03

Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford has revealed it was a "horrendous feeling" not to play regularly for Manchester City last term.

The 27-year-old worked his way through the Man City academy system before spending time out on loan with Accrington Stanley and Bolton Wanderers.

Trafford eventually completed a permanent move to Burnley, where he impressed during his two-year spell to earn him a return to Manchester City last summer.

However, his hopes of being Man City's first-choice goalkeeper were dashed when Gianluigi Donnarumma joined the club on the final day of the summer transfer window.

As a result, Trafford did not make a single Premier League appearance from the end of August until he was handed the chance to start the final game of the season against Aston Villa.

Trafford's Man City return ultimately lasted just one season as his desire to enjoy regular playing time saw him complete a move to Leeds United in the summer.

The 24-year-old has now opened up on the "horrendous feeling" he got from not playing regularly under Pep Guardiola last time.

"What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing," Trafford told BBC Sport.  "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up.

"I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny.

"I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing.

"Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous.

"I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve."

Trafford at least managed to help Man City win the EFL Cup and FA Cup in Guardiola's final season at the Etihad Stadium.

The England international recorded four shutouts in six EFL Cup games and three clean sheets in six FA Cup matches.

"Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens," Trafford added.

"In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year.

"There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

Trafford has since got his wish of being a Premier League number one, having recorded three clean sheets in Leeds' nine top-flight games this term.

The Man City academy product will feature in the lunchtime kickoff against Tottenham Hotspur before he links up with Thomas Tuchel's England squad, where he is continuing to compete with Jordan Pickford for the number one spot.
